  원심의 위와 같은 판단 또한 앞서 본 법리에 비추어 모두 정당하고, 거기에 상고이유로 주장하는 바와 같은 채증법칙 위반 등의 위법은 없다.
  라. 원심은 그 설시의 증거들을 종합하여, 이 사건에서 원고 2가 피고 병원에 내원하기 이전에 이미 쌍태아 중 일측 태아의 사망으로 생존 태아에게 비가역적인 뇌손상이 발생하였을 가능성이 크다고 인정한 후, 원고 1의 뇌성마비 발생에 대하여 피고 병원 의료진의 의료행위 이외에 다른 원인이 개재될 수 없다는 점을 원고들이 입증하지 못하고 있는 이상, 피고들의 과실과 원고 1의 뇌성마비 사이의 인과관계를 추정할 수 없다고 판단하였다.
  원심의 위 판단도 앞서 본 의료소송에 있어서 인과관계의 추정에 관한 법리에 따른 것으로서 정당하고, 거기에 채증법칙 위반 등의 위법이 없다.
  2. 설명의무 위반에 대하여

neutral_fact_en: [COMPANY_A] hired [COMPANY_B] in 2004 to relocate a gas pipeline on a large tract of wooded, unimproved land. On August 7, 2004, [COMPANY_B] drove a small bulldozer, with its blade raised off the ground, through an area containing grave sites. The plaintiffs alleged that the graves were not indicated on any map, identified in a deed, marked by an obvious sign, included on a government-maintained list, or otherwise reasonably identifiable as an area containing graves. [COMPANY_B] contended that the area was significantly overgrown, contained mostly unmarked grave sites, and had some grave markers buried in forest debris. After the bulldozer operator realized that the bulldozer had passed through the grave-site area, he immediately blocked off the area and relocated the route to connect with the pipeline at a different location. Six plaintiffs claimed that their decedent was buried directly beneath the bulldozer's path, and two others stated that they believed their decedent could be buried beneath that path; however, the plaintiffs' expert was unable to locate a grave shaft directly under the path.

neutral_fact_source: [COMPANY_A] hired [COMPANY_B] in 2004 to relocate a gas pipeline on a large tract of wooded, unimproved land. On August 7, 2004, [COMPANY_B] drove a small bulldozer, with its blade raised off the ground, through an area containing grave sites. The plaintiffs alleged that the graves were not indicated on any map, identified in a deed, marked by an obvious sign, included on a government-maintained list, or otherwise reasonably identifiable as an area containing graves. [COMPANY_B] contended that the area was significantly overgrown, contained mostly unmarked grave sites, and had some grave markers buried in forest debris. aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [PERSON_A] was a tenant at [PROPERTY_A], a complex owned by [COMPANY_A] and [COMPANY_B]. On June 25, 1999, after returning home from work, [PERSON_A] took [ANIMAL_A] for a walk around the apartment complex. During the walk, [PERSON_A] and [ANIMAL_A] traversed a sidewalk in a common area of the complex. The grass strip was approximately 3.35 meters wide and was elevated above the parking lot approximately 1.22 meters. The grass strip was supported laterally by a white brick retaining wall, and there was no fence or other structure along the edge of the retaining wall. As [PERSON_A] and [ANIMAL_A] walked along the sidewalk, a girl in a nearby apartment unexpectedly let [ANIMAL_B] out of her apartment. [ANIMAL_B] were larger than [ANIMAL_A], and they rushed toward [PERSON_A] and [ANIMAL_A] snarling and snapping. [PERSON_A] quickly retreated backwards to pull [ANIMAL_A] away from the attacking [ANIMAL_B]. [PERSON_A] moved off of the sidewalk and across the grass strip. In her haste, she backed up to the edge of the grass strip, stumbled over the edge of the retaining wall, and fell onto the parking lot below. After falling onto the parking lot below, [PERSON_A] suffered fractures to a rib, a hip, and a femur. Construction of the retaining wall had been completed in 1987, and the retaining wall had remained structurally unchanged since that time. [COMPANY_A] and [COMPANY_B] were not the original owners of the apartment complex. [PERSON_A] alleged that [COMPANY_A] and [COMPANY_B] had failed to design, build, and maintain a reasonably safe retaining wall and had failed to warn her about the hazard. [PERSON_A] alleged medical expenses of [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A], as well as loss of income and pain and suffering, resulting from the incident. [COMPANY_A] and [COMPANY_B] characterized the retaining wall as an improvement completed more than ten years before [PERSON_A]'s injury.

[PERSON_A]와 [ANIMAL_A]가 보도를 따라 걷고 있을 때, 인근 아파트에 있던 한 소녀가 갑자기 자신의 아파트에서 [ANIMAL_B]를 내보냈다. [ANIMAL_B]는 [ANIMAL_A]보다 컸고, 으르렁거리며 이빨을 드러낸 채 [PERSON_A]와 [ANIMAL_A]를 향해 달려들었다. [PERSON_A]는 공격하는 [ANIMAL_B]로부터 [ANIMAL_A]를 떼어 놓기 위해 재빨리 뒤로 물러났다. [PERSON_A]는 보도에서 벗어나 잔디 띠를 가로질러 이동했다. 서두르던 중 [PERSON_A]는 잔디 띠의 가장자리까지 뒤로 물러났고, 옹벽 가장자리에 걸려 아래 주차장으로 떨어졌다. 아래 주차장으로 떨어진 후, [PERSON_A]는 갈비뼈, 엉덩관절 및 대퇴골에 골절을 입었다. 옹벽의 건설은 1987년에 완료되었고, 옹벽은 그때부터 구조적으로 변경되지 않은 상태로 유지되었다. [COMPANY_A]와 [COMPANY_B]는 아파트 단지의 최초 소유자가 아니었다. [PERSON_A]는 [COMPANY_A]와 [COMPANY_B]가 합리적으로 안전한 옹벽을 설계하고 건설하며 유지관리하지 못했고, 자신에게 위험을 경고하지 못했다고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]는 해당 사건으로 인해 [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A]의 의료비와 소득 손실 및 고통과 고생이 발생했다고 주장했다. [COMPANY_A]와 [COMPANY_B]는 해당 옹벽을 [PERSON_A]의 부상 발생 시점보다 10년 넘게 전에 완공된 개선 시설로 규정했다.

We conclude that full recovery for actual losses includes not only the converted inventory, but also resulting damages such as the value of a lost business. FACTS Appellant/cross-respondent Calvin Winchell, d/b/a CGL Seafood, Inc., owned and operated a wholesale fresh fish business in Las Vegas, Nevada. Winchell’s business grew from $36,780 in sales in 1996 to $759,711 in 2000. With such dramatic growth, *942Winchell was in need of a much larger storage facility for his inventory.

source_fact_units.model_source_span: Respondent/cross-appellant Renate Schiff, Trustee of Schiff Properties, owned a cold storage facility and offered to lease a portion of that space to Winchell. Winchell accepted her offer, and the parties executed a two-year lease agreement that expired in December 2000. source_fact_units.model_source_span: A few months before the lease was set to expire, on August 21, 2000, while Winchell was out of town, Schiff s property manager, Beryl Duncan, became concerned that Winchell may have abandoned the premises. Having had prior experience with tenants abandoning cold storage units, turning the power off, and leaving unrefrigerated fish behind, Duncan was apparently concerned about whether the electricity had been shut off. Accordingly, Duncan attempted to contact Winchell by telephone, to no avail. Duncan subsequently determined that it was necessary to inspect the storage unit. To gain access into the unit, Duncan hired a locksmith and directed him to drill out and replace the locks.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: On January 26, 1991, [PERSON_A] was a passenger in [VEHICLE_A], which was operated by [PERSON_B]. [VEHICLE_A] was proceeding east on [LOCATION_A] when it fishtailed on the snow-covered roadway. The fishtailing caused [PERSON_B] to lose control of [VEHICLE_A]; [VEHICLE_A] then left the graveled portion of the highway, traveled over [LOCATION_B], and overturned. [PERSON_A] sustained serious injuries resulting in quadriplegia. [PERSON_A] alleged that [ORGANIZATION_A] failed to shield the steep embankment with a guardrail at the accident location and failed to properly design, construct, and maintain the highway. [PERSON_A] further alleged that [ORGANIZATION_A] failed to comply with accepted industry or government standards for highway design, construction, maintenance, repair, and guarding; failed to replace previously existing guardrails that had been removed; failed to flatten the severe embankment; and failed to comply with its own and federal highway design and maintenance rules. [PERSON_A] alleged that prevailing engineering standards required guardrails at this location because of the road's curvature and the proximity of [LOCATION_B]. [PERSON_A] alleged that, without a guardrail, an occupant of a vehicle leaving the paved surface would suffer more serious injuries by traveling down [LOCATION_B] than if a guardrail halted the impact. [ORGANIZATION_A] characterized the roadway property as merely facilitating the injury, while [PERSON_A] characterized the lack of a guardrail on the highway, rather than [LOCATION_B], as the defective condition.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: On February 4, 2002, [PERSON_A] was driving [VEHICLE_A] when it went out of control and rolled over; [PERSON_A] was injured, and [VEHICLE_A] was insured by [COMPANY_B]. Representatives of [COMPANY_B] inspected [VEHICLE_A], determined it was a total loss, received ownership documents from [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B], paid them [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A], and sold [VEHICLE_A] to [COMPANY_D] on April 11, 2002; [VEHICLE_A] was apparently broken apart and sold for parts and scrap. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] alleged that [VEHICLE_A]'s suspension was defectively designed, making it inherently unstable and insufficiently resistant to rollover. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] apparently discovered that removal of some of [VEHICLE_A]'s suspension parts by [COMPANY_E] impaired their product-liability lawsuit. [COMPANY_B] argued that, when [VEHICLE_A] was sold to the salvage yard, there was no evidence that [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] had filed or were contemplating a civil action, or that [COMPANY_B] knew of such an action. [COMPANY_B] had processed approximately 500 claims involving [VEHICLE_A] models in the preceding ten years, and those claims cost approximately [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_B] in total. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] argued that [COMPANY_B]'s prior payments and earlier action demonstrated knowledge of [VEHICLE_A]'s alleged defect and tendency to roll over, while [COMPANY_B] argued that the record did not show that it knew the rollover was caused by a defect or that [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] intended to sue [COMPANY_A]. [PERSON_B] testified that, during dealings with [COMPANY_B] about the collision claim involving [VEHICLE_A], he did not tell any representative that he was going to sue [COMPANY_A] or was thinking about suing [COMPANY_A].

[VEHICLE_A]는 분해되어 부품과 고철로 판매된 것으로 보인다. [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]는 [VEHICLE_A]의 서스펜션이 결함 있게 설계되어 차량이 본질적으로 불안정하고 전복에 대한 저항력이 불충분하다고 주장했다. liability_theories: failure to properly maintain and repair a window screen
property-owner/custodian liability under La. C.C. art. 2317.1
neutral_fact_en: [PERSON_A] was [PERSON_B]'s daughter. On March 30, 1996, two-and-a-half-year-old [PERSON_A] fell from a second-floor window of her apartment building and landed on a first-floor balcony. After the fall, [PERSON_A] was treated for a depressed skull fracture, a hematoma of the upper eyelid, a forehead laceration, a left nondisplaced frontal fracture, and a broken left arm and wrist. [PERSON_B] alleged that [ORGANIZATION_A] failed to properly maintain and repair the window screen in [PERSON_A]'s bedroom and that this caused [PERSON_A]'s injuries. [PERSON_B] testified that around noon on the date of the accident, she put [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_A]'s five-year-old sister down for a nap, opened one bedroom window because the air-conditioning unit in the other window was not working, and went to her own bedroom to sleep. [PERSON_B] testified that 30–45 minutes later, her older daughter screamed that [PERSON_A] had fallen out of the bedroom window; [PERSON_B] entered the bedroom, saw the screen hanging from the top to one side, and saw [PERSON_A] lying on the first-floor balcony below. [PERSON_B] testified that no screen had been on the window for the eight to nine years she lived in the apartment, and that an [ORGANIZATION_A] employee named [PERSON_D] installed a screen two to three days before the accident after she requested one. [PERSON_B] acknowledged signing an [ORGANIZATION_A] work order dated November 25, 1995 for screen installation, approximately five months before the accident. [PERSON_B] testified that the screen appeared properly installed when she opened the window, that she did not know whether it was locked at the bottom before the accident, and that she had not notified [ORGANIZATION_A] that it was improperly installed. [PERSON_C] testified that she saw [PERSON_A] fall out of the window but did not see what caused the fall because [PERSON_A] was already coming out of the window when she looked up. [PERSON_D] testified that the screen was installed on November 25, 1995 by a maintenance crew brought in from other housing developments. [PERSON_D] testified that the maintenance file contained no [ORGANIZATION_A] work request or order from March 1996, that he did not recall installing the screen, and that an order bearing his name would have existed if he had installed it. [PERSON_E] testified that the screens were intended to be decorative and to keep insects out when the window was raised, not to prevent children from falling out. [PERSON_E] testified that the screens fit into two slats on the outside of the window casing and were held in place by two hooks that went over two small pins; he also testified that a maintenance ticket indicated installation in November 1995. [PERSON_E] testified that he never inspected the particular window screen, and a new screen was installed the day after the accident. [PERSON_A]'s treating physician testified that he treated her for excessive bed-wetting on March 5, 1998, believed it was caused by continued urinary tract infections associated with poor hygiene, and testified that the lack of blood in her urine and the [LOCATION_JURISDICTION]-scan results indicated no urinary-tract trauma from the fall.
neutral_fact_ko: [PERSON_A]는 [PERSON_B]의 딸이었다. 1996년 3월 30일, 두 살 반이었던 [PERSON_A]는 자신이 사는 아파트 건물의 2층 창문에서 떨어져 1층 발코니에 떨어졌다. 추락 후 [PERSON_A]는 함몰성 두개골 골절, 위쪽 눈꺼풀 혈종, 이마 열상, 왼쪽 비전위성 전두골 골절, 그리고 왼쪽 팔과 손목 골절에 대한 치료를 받았다. [PERSON_B]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 [PERSON_A]의 침실 창문 방충망을 적절히 유지·보수하지 않았으며 이로 인해 [PERSON_A]의 부상이 발생했다고 주장했다. [PERSON_B]는 사고 당일 정오 무렵 [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_A]의 다섯 살 난 언니를 낮잠 자게 하고, 다른 창문의 에어컨이 작동하지 않았기 때문에 침실 창문 하나를 열었으며, 자신이 자는 침실로 가서 잠을 잤다고 증언했다. [PERSON_B]는 30~45분 후 자신의 큰딸이 [PERSON_A]가 침실 창문 밖으로 떨어졌다고 소리쳤고, [PERSON_B]가 침실에 들어가 방충망이 위쪽에서 한쪽으로 매달려 있는 것을 보았으며, 아래 1층 발코니에 [PERSON_A]가 누워 있는 것을 보았다고 증언했다. [PERSON_B]는 자신이 그 아파트에 거주한 8~9년 동안 창문에 방충망이 없었으며, 방충망을 요청한 후 사고 이틀 내지 사흘 전에 [PERSON_D]라는 [ORGANIZATION_A] 직원이 방충망을 설치했다고 증언했다. [PERSON_B]는 사고 약 5개월 전인 1995년 11월 25일자로 방충망 설치를 위해 작성된 [ORGANIZATION_A] 작업 지시서에 서명한 사실을 인정했다. [PERSON_B]는 창문을 열었을 때 방충망이 적절히 설치된 것처럼 보였고, 사고 전에 방충망 하단이 잠겨 있었는지는 몰랐으며, 방충망이 부적절하게 설치되었다고 [ORGANIZATION_A]에 알리지 않았다고 증언했다. [PERSON_C]는 [PERSON_A]가 창문 밖으로 떨어지는 것을 보았지만, 고개를 들었을 때 [PERSON_A]가 이미 창문 밖으로 나오고 있었기 때문에 추락을 일으킨 원인은 보지 못했다고 증언했다. [PERSON_D]는 방충망이 1995년 11월 25일 다른 주택 개발 지역에서 데려온 유지보수 작업반에 의해 설치되었다고 증언했다. [PERSON_D]는 유지보수 파일에 1996년 3월의 [ORGANIZATION_A] 작업 요청서나 작업 지시서가 없었고, 자신이 방충망을 설치한 기억이 없으며, 자신이 설치했다면 자신의 이름이 기재된 지시서가 존재했을 것이라고 증언했다. [PERSON_E]는 방충망이 장식용이며 창문을 올렸을 때 벌레가 들어오지 못하게 하기 위한 것이지, 아이들이 밖으로 떨어지는 것을 방지하기 위한 것은 아니었다고 증언했다. [PERSON_E]는 방충망이 창틀 바깥쪽의 두 개 홈에 끼워지고, 두 개의 작은 핀 위로 걸치는 두 개의 고리로 제자리에 고정되었다고 증언했다. 또한 유지보수 작업표에 1995년 11월 설치로 표시되어 있었다고 증언했다. [PERSON_E]는 해당 창문의 방충망을 검사한 적이 전혀 없으며, 사고 다음 날 새 방충망이 설치되었다고 증언했다. [PERSON_A]의 담당 의사는 1998년 3월 5일 [PERSON_A]의 과도한 야뇨를 치료했고, 그것이 위생 불량과 관련된 지속적인 요로 감염으로 인해 발생했다고 믿었으며, [PERSON_A]의 소변에 혈액이 없고 [LOCATION_JURISDICTION]-스캔 결과가 추락으로 인한 요로 외상을 나타내지 않았다고 증언했다.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: In May 1991, [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_E] purchased a used [PRODUCT_A] from a dealership. In addition to gasoline propulsion engines, [PRODUCT_A] contained a small [PRODUCT_B] that powered its accessories, including the [PRODUCT_C]. On May 29, 1993, during a weekend cruise at [LOCATION_A], [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] secured [PRODUCT_A] alongside a beach, went to sleep in its cabin, and left [PRODUCT_B] running to power [PRODUCT_C]. The next morning, [PERSON_F], a friend staying at the beach, knocked on the cabin door and received no response; later that afternoon, [PERSON_F] boarded [PRODUCT_A] and found [PERSON_A] dead and [PERSON_B] barely breathing. [PERSON_F] testified that the engines were not running during either check, and a subsequent investigation identified [PRODUCT_B], rather than the engines, as the source of the carbon monoxide, which is tasteless and odorless. [PERSON_A] died and [PERSON_B] suffered catastrophic injuries from carbon monoxide poisoning during an overnight outing in [PRODUCT_A] at [LOCATION_A]. The injuries suffered by [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] were caused by odorless and tasteless carbon monoxide fumes from [PRODUCT_B], which powered [PRODUCT_C], rather than by exhaust fumes. Two warnings about carbon monoxide poisoning accompanied the sale of this type of [PRODUCT_A] in 1981: one was written by [ORGANIZATION_A], the generator manufacturer, and the other by [ORGANIZATION_B]. [COMPANY_A] also provided purchasers with other manuals. Both warnings primarily addressed carbon monoxide exposure from engine exhaust. When [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_E] purchased [PRODUCT_A], the dealership service manager, [PERSON_G], and salesperson, [PERSON_H], warned them about exhaust fumes and carbon monoxide and the need to ventilate [PRODUCT_A] to remove hazardous fumes. [PERSON_G] and [PERSON_H] demonstrated flow-through ventilation by opening a window and the hatch, explained that the rear door should remain open when the main propulsion engines were running, and [PERSON_G] stated that idling the engine with the front hatch closed could cause carbon monoxide to accumulate. [PERSON_B], [PERSON_C], and [PERSON_D] alleged that "migrating carbon monoxide" caused the incident when carbon monoxide safely exhausted from [PRODUCT_B] into the open air was blown back into [PRODUCT_A] by wind and entered the passenger cabin through small openings. [COMPANY_A]'s expert agreed with this causal explanation but testified that the phenomenon was rare and that ventilation in the passenger cabin had to be obstructed for carbon monoxide to accumulate to dangerous levels. The expert identified three precautions: posting a watch because carbon monoxide detection devices were unavailable in 1981; anchoring [PRODUCT_A] from the bow rather than the side so wind currents would blow away from the stern; or creating flow-through ventilation before sleeping. The expert conceded that [COMPANY_A]'s manual contained none of those instructions or warnings, but testified that no death-causing incident of that type had been reported for the particular [PRODUCT_A] model involved.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: 1991년 5월, [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_E]는 판매점에서 중고 [PRODUCT_A]를 구입했다. [PRODUCT_A]에는 가솔린 추진 엔진 외에도 [PRODUCT_C]를 포함한 부속 장치에 동력을 공급하는 소형 [PRODUCT_B]가 들어 있었다. 1993년 5월 29일, [LOCATION_A]에서 주말 항해를 하던 중 [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]는 해변 옆에 [PRODUCT_A]를 계류하고 그 선실에서 잠들었으며, [PRODUCT_C]에 동력을 공급하기 위해 [PRODUCT_B]를 작동시킨 채로 두었다. 다음 날 아침, 해변에 머물고 있던 친구 [PERSON_F]는 선실 문을 두드렸으나 응답을 받지 못했다. 그날 오후 늦게 [PERSON_F]는 [PRODUCT_A]에 올라 [PERSON_A]가 사망해 있고 [PERSON_B]가 간신히 숨을 쉬고 있는 것을 발견했다. [PERSON_F]는 두 차례 확인 당시 엔진이 작동하고 있지 않았다고 증언했으며, 이후 조사에서는 무색무취인 일산화탄소의 원인이 엔진이 아니라 [PRODUCT_B]인 것으로 확인되었다. [LOCATION_A]에서 [PRODUCT_A]로 하룻밤 외출을 하는 동안 일산화탄소 중독으로 [PERSON_A]는 사망했고 [PERSON_B]는 치명적인 부상을 입었다. [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]가 입은 부상은 배기가스가 아니라 [PRODUCT_C]에 동력을 공급하던 [PRODUCT_B]에서 나온 무취·무미의 일산화탄소 가스로 인해 발생했다. 1981년에 이러한 유형의 [PRODUCT_A]가 판매될 때 일산화탄소 중독에 관한 두 가지 경고가 함께 제공되었다. 하나는 발전기 제조업체인 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 작성했고, 다른 하나는 [ORGANIZATION_B]가 작성했다. [COMPANY_A]는 구매자들에게 다른 설명서도 제공했다. 두 경고는 모두 주로 엔진 배기가스로 인한 일산화탄소 노출을 다루었다. [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_E]가 [PRODUCT_A]를 구입할 당시, 판매점의 서비스 관리자 [PERSON_G]와 영업사원 [PERSON_H]는 배기가스와 일산화탄소, 그리고 위험한 가스를 제거하기 위해 [PRODUCT_A]를 환기해야 할 필요성에 대해 이들에게 경고했다. [PERSON_G]와 [PERSON_H]는 창문과 해치를 열어 공기가 통과하는 환기를 시연했고, 주 추진 엔진이 작동할 때는 뒷문을 열어 둬야 한다고 설명했으며, [PERSON_G]는 앞쪽 해치를 닫은 채 엔진을 공회전시키면 일산화탄소가 축적될 수 있다고 말했다. [PERSON_B], [PERSON_C], [PERSON_D]는 [PRODUCT_B]에서 일산화탄소가 안전하게 대기 중으로 배출되었지만 바람에 의해 [PRODUCT_A] 안으로 다시 불어 들어와 작은 틈을 통해 승객 선실에 유입되면서 "이동하는 일산화탄소"가 사건을 일으켰다고 주장했다. [COMPANY_A]의 전문가는 이러한 인과관계 설명에 동의했지만, 그 현상은 드물며 일산화탄소가 위험한 수준으로 축적되려면 승객 선실의 환기가 막혀 있어야 한다고 증언했다. 전문가는 세 가지 예방조치를 제시했다. 1981년에는 일산화탄소 감지 장치를 사용할 수 없었으므로 감시자를 배치하는 것, 바람의 흐름이 선미에서 멀어지는 방향으로 불도록 [PRODUCT_A]를 측면이 아니라 선수에서 계류하는 것, 또는 잠들기 전에 공기가 통과하는 환기를 만드는 것이었다. 전문가는 [COMPANY_A]의 설명서에 그러한 지침이나 경고가 전혀 포함되어 있지 않았다는 점을 인정했지만, 관련된 특정 [PRODUCT_A] 모델에서 그러한 유형의 사망을 초래한 사건은 보고된 적이 없다고 증언했다.

neutral_fact_source: In May 1991, [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_E] purchased a used [PRODUCT_A] from a dealership. In addition to gasoline propulsion engines, [PRODUCT_A] contained a small [PRODUCT_B] that powered its accessories, including the [PRODUCT_C]. On May 29, 1993, during a weekend cruise at [LOCATION_A], [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] secured [PRODUCT_A] alongside a beach, went to sleep in its cabin, and left [PRODUCT_B] running to power [PRODUCT_C]. The next morning, [PERSON_F], a friend staying at the beach, knocked on the cabin door and received no response; later that afternoon, [PERSON_F] boarded [PRODUCT_A] and found [PERSON_A] dead and [PERSON_B] barely breathing. [PERSON_F] testified that the engines were not running during either check, and a subsequent investigation identified [PRODUCT_B], rather than the engines, as the source of the carbon monoxide, which is tasteless and odorless. [PERSON_A] died and [PERSON_B] suffered catastrophic injuries from carbon monoxide poisoning during an overnight outing in [PRODUCT_A] at [LOCATION_A]. The injuries suffered by [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] were caused by odorless and tasteless carbon monoxide fumes from [PRODUCT_B], which powered [PRODUCT_C], rather than by exhaust fumes. Two warnings about carbon monoxide poisoning accompanied the sale of this type of [PRODUCT_A] in 1981: one was written by [ORGANIZATION_A], the generator manufacturer, and the other by [ORGANIZATION_B]. [COMPANY_A] also provided purchasers with other manuals. Both warnings primarily addressed carbon monoxide exposure from engine exhaust. When [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_E] purchased [PRODUCT_A], the dealership service manager, [PERSON_G], and salesperson, [PERSON_H], warned them about exhaust fumes and carbon monoxide and the need to ventilate [PRODUCT_A] to remove hazardous fumes. [PERSON_G] and [PERSON_H] demonstrated flow-through ventilation by opening a window and the hatch, explained that the rear door should remain open when the main propulsion engines were running, and [PERSON_G] stated that idling the engine with the front hatch closed could cause carbon monoxide to accumulate. [PERSON_B], [PERSON_C], and [PERSON_D] alleged that "migrating carbon monoxide" caused the incident when carbon monoxide safely exhausted from [PRODUCT_B] into the open air was blown back into [PRODUCT_A] by wind and entered the passenger cabin through small openings. [COMPANY_A]'s expert agreed with this causal explanation but testified that the phenomenon was rare and that ventilation in the passenger cabin had to be obstructed for carbon monoxide to accumulate to dangerous levels. The expert identified three precautions: posting a watch because carbon monoxide detection devices were unavailable in 1981; anchoring [PRODUCT_A] from the bow rather than the side so wind currents would blow away from the stern; or creating flow-through ventilation before sleeping. The expert conceded that [COMPANY_A]'s manual contained none of those instructions or warnings, but testified that no death-causing incident of that type had been reported for the particular [PRODUCT_A] model involved.

neutral_fact_en: [COMPANY_A] was Mid-[LOCATION_JURISDICTION] Valley Medical Corp., also known as Mid-[LOCATION_JURISDICTION] Valley Urgent Care; [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] were the Arbogasts. On March 26, 1996, [PERSON_C], a laboratory technician employed by [COMPANY_A], drew blood from [PERSON_A]’s left arm for a complete blood count. On April 1, 1996, [PERSON_A] had a bruise, pain, and numbness in her left hand. [PERSON_D] diagnosed a hematoma of her left arm. On April 8, 1996, she continued to have pain and numbness in her left arm and hand, and the hematoma was still present. [PERSON_E]’s April 9, 1996 medical note described pain from the needle stick, a possible small hematoma, and pressure on a nerve. The follow-up testing documented questionable, very mild carpal tunnel syndrome. On July 12, 1996, [PERSON_F]’s medical notes ruled out signs of early or late complex regional pain syndrome and stated that all of [PERSON_A]’s forearm and hand muscles functioned normally. [PERSON_F] could not definitively diagnose the cause of her pain. [PERSON_F] recommended nerve-release surgery at the left forearm and carpal-tunnel-release surgery at the left wrist. The surgery was performed on August 21, 1996. [PERSON_A] continued to experience pain and numbness afterward; on March 7, 1997, her left arm was purplish and cold, which [PERSON_F] indicated might be an early sign of complex regional pain syndrome. On July 29, 1997, [PERSON_G] diagnosed [PERSON_A] as suffering from complex regional pain syndrome. [PERSON_J] testified that it was unclear whether he was referring to a national or local standard. [PERSON_A] sat on the edge of an examining table and held out her left arm with her hand against the inside of her left knee. No support stabilized her arm before a needle was inserted. [PERSON_K] opined that the needle insertion did not damage the nerve in [PERSON_A]’s arm. [PERSON_G] conceded that the carpal-tunnel surgery performed by [PERSON_F] could have caused complex regional pain syndrome, and [PERSON_H] acknowledged that the surgery could have contributed to its development. [PERSON_A] alleged that the needle damaged a median vein in her arm, resulting in her developing complex regional pain syndrome. [PERSON_A] testified that needle insertion caused excruciating pain. [PERSON_G] stated that the EMG results did not conclusively assess the area where the needle was inserted and opined that a thorough examination there might have revealed nerve damage; he also opined that the complex regional pain syndrome resulted from nerve damage caused by the needle insertion. [PERSON_I] testified that she would expect a patient to complain if median-nerve damage caused the type of pain [PERSON_A] experienced. [PERSON_K] testified that if a median nerve had been struck, [PERSON_A] would have jumped, screamed, or called attention to it.

[PERSON_F]은 [PERSON_A]의 통증 원인을 확정적으로 진단할 수 없었다. [PERSON_J]은 자신이 국가적 기준을 말한 것인지 지역적 기준을 말한 것인지 불분명하다고 증언했다. [PERSON_A]는 진찰대 가장자리에 앉아 왼손을 왼쪽 무릎 안쪽에 대고 왼쪽 팔을 내밀었다. 바늘이 삽입되기 전에 [PERSON_A]의 팔을 안정시키는 지지대는 없었다. [PERSON_K]은 바늘 삽입이 [PERSON_A]의 팔에 있는 신경을 손상시키지 않았다고 의견을 제시했다. [PERSON_G]은 [PERSON_F]이 시행한 손목터널 수술이 복합부위통증증후군을 유발했을 수 있다고 인정했으며, [PERSON_H]는 그 수술이 복합부위통증증후군의 발생에 기여했을 수 있다고 인정했다. [PERSON_A]는 바늘이 자신의 팔에 있는 정중정맥을 손상시켜 그 결과 복합부위통증증후군이 발생했다고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]는 바늘 삽입으로 극심한 통증이 발생했다고 증언했다. [PERSON_G]은 근전도검사 결과가 바늘이 삽입된 부위를 결정적으로 평가하지 못했다고 말했으며, 그 부위를 철저히 검사했다면 신경 손상이 드러났을 수도 있다고 의견을 제시했다. 또한 [PERSON_G]은 복합부위통증증후군이 바늘 삽입으로 발생한 신경 손상에서 비롯되었다고 의견을 제시했다. [PERSON_I]는 정중신경 손상으로 [PERSON_A]가 경험한 유형의 통증이 발생했다면 환자가 불평할 것으로 예상한다고 증언했다. [PERSON_K]은 정중신경이 찔렸다면 [PERSON_A]가 움찔하거나 소리를 지르거나 그 사실에 주의를 환기했을 것이라고 증언했다.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [PERSON_A] was traveling westbound on [LOCATION_A] and attempted a left turn at a permissive green light to proceed southbound on [LOCATION_B]. At the same time, [ORGANIZATION_A] Officer [PERSON_B] was driving his patrol vehicle eastbound on [LOCATION_A] approaching [LOCATION_B]. The speed limit on [LOCATION_A] was 72.42 km/h, but Officer [PERSON_B] was traveling between 93.34 km/h and 119.09 km/h. Officer [PERSON_B] did not have his police siren or lights activated. [PERSON_A] apparently did not realize how fast Officer [PERSON_B] was approaching and entered the intersection without enough time to clear it. Officer [PERSON_B] slammed on his brakes, but the two cars collided. As a result of the collision, [PERSON_A] suffered multiple internal injuries and trauma to his brain stem. After spending three weeks in a coma, [PERSON_A] died. A blood sample drawn from [PERSON_A] hours after the crash revealed a BAC of .049 percent, and no blood sample was drawn from or tested for alcohol or other substances for Officer [PERSON_B] after the crash. [PERSON_C], individually and as representative of [PERSON_A]’s estate, and [PERSON_A]’s son and two daughters alleged that [ORGANIZATION_A] and Officer [PERSON_B]’s conduct resulted in [PERSON_A]’s death. [ORGANIZATION_A] asserted that [PERSON_A]’s injuries were caused by his own conduct, which [ORGANIZATION_A] described as greater than any negligent conduct by Officer [PERSON_B]. The experts disagreed about how far above the speed limit Officer [PERSON_B] was traveling, but all experts agreed that [PERSON_A] would have passed through the intersection with time to spare if Officer [PERSON_B] had been traveling at the posted speed limit.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [PERSON_A], a two-month-old child, died while under the care of pediatrician [PERSON_D] and staff members of [COMPANY_A], [PERSON_D]’s employer. [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C], the child’s parents, brought [PERSON_A] to [PERSON_D] for multiple visits after his birth and contacted [PERSON_D]’s office seven times during the week before his death. On July 27, [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C] reported to [PERSON_D] that [PERSON_A] was taking only about 118 milliliters of formula instead of the customary 177 or 207 milliliters, cried after feedings, and had a slight cough. On July 29, [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C] reported to [COMPANY_A]’s telephone service and later to [PERSON_D] that [PERSON_A] had projectile vomiting, had been fussy for five days, and was tired after feeding. [PERSON_D] considered pyloric stenosis and noted that a barium swallow test might be indicated, but did not order the test after later developments discounted that diagnosis. On July 30, [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C] reported that [PERSON_A] continued to have a slight cough and had vomited two or three times daily for four or five days. On August 1, they reported that he was fussy, sometimes vomiting, not sleeping, experiencing pain while feeding, and wheezy afterward. [PERSON_D] considered the symptoms consistent with gastroesophageal reflux, prescribed medication for that condition, and immunized [PERSON_A]. On August 2, [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C] reported that [PERSON_A]’s formula consumption had dropped to about 89 milliliters, that he was fussy, not sleeping, and screaming as if in pain, that he had wet only two diapers, and that he had a temperature of 38.3°C despite receiving Tylenol every four hours. [PERSON_D] considered the symptoms consistent with reactions to the previous day’s immunizations and possible acid-reflux pain. On August 3, [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C] took [PERSON_A] to [INSTITUTION_A], where [PERSON_E] found him in severe respiratory distress and confirmed that his heart rate was dangerously low. Despite intubation, ventilation, and other supportive measures, [PERSON_A] died during the early morning of August 4. aligned_fact_units.source_text: [PERSON_A], a two-month-old child, died while under the care of pediatrician [PERSON_D] and staff members of [COMPANY_A], [PERSON_D]’s employer. On July 27, [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C] reported to [PERSON_D] that [PERSON_A] was taking only about 118 milliliters of formula instead of the customary 177 or 207 milliliters, cried after feedings, and had a slight cough. On July 29, [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C] reported to [COMPANY_A]’s telephone service and later to [PERSON_D] that [PERSON_A] had projectile vomiting, had been fussy for five days, and was tired after feeding. [PERSON_D] considered pyloric stenosis and noted that a barium swallow test might be indicated, but did not order the test after later developments discounted that diagnosis. On July 30, [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C] reported that [PERSON_A] continued to have a slight cough and had vomited two or three times daily for four or five days. On August 1, they reported that he was fussy, sometimes vomiting, not sleeping, experiencing pain while feeding, and wheezy afterward. [PERSON_D] considered the symptoms consistent with gastroesophageal reflux, prescribed medication for that condition, and immunized [PERSON_A]. On August 2, [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C] reported that [PERSON_A]’s formula consumption had dropped to about 89 milliliters, that he was fussy, not sleeping, and screaming as if in pain, that he had wet only two diapers, and that he had a temperature of 38.3°C despite receiving Tylenol every four hours. [PERSON_D] considered the symptoms consistent with reactions to the previous day’s immunizations and possible acid-reflux pain. On August 3, [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C] took [PERSON_A] to [INSTITUTION_A], where [PERSON_E] found him in severe respiratory distress and confirmed that his heart rate was dangerously low. Despite intubation, ventilation, and other supportive measures, [PERSON_A] died during the early morning of August 4. A postmortem examination established that [PERSON_A]’s death was caused by diffuse acute viral myocarditis, a viral infection of the heart muscle.

source_fact_units.model_source_span: Facts & Background The plaintiff, Naomi McDavid, on her own behalf and as the personal representative of her deceased husband, Oney McDavid ("the decedent"), contends that in October 1999, the decedent received an x-ray at the Veterans Administration Medical Center in Huntington ("VA hospital"). The x-ray revealed an opacity on the decedent's right lung. According to the plaintiff, the decedent was told not to worry about the opacity and no further tests were ordered at that time. In January 2000, the decedent went to his family doctor complaining of a cough. At that time, an x-ray revealed that the opacity had tripled in size. It was subsequently discovered to be cancerous.

neutral_fact_en: [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_C] had a three-year-long relationship. Near the conclusion of the relationship, [PERSON_A] became pregnant, and she told [PERSON_C] that the pregnancy was achieved via artificial insemination and that he was not the father of [PERSON_E]. [PERSON_E] was born in March 2001. In August 2010, suspecting he might be [PERSON_E]’s father, [PERSON_C] initiated a paternity proceeding. DNA testing revealed that he was [PERSON_E]’s father, and on September 11, 2011, [PERSON_C] announced his paternity on Facebook. [PERSON_C] claimed that [PERSON_A] actively, fraudulently, knowingly, and intentionally concealed his paternity from him and interfered with his efforts to establish a relationship with [PERSON_E]. [PERSON_A] retained [PERSON_B] to represent her. [PERSON_B] asserted that [PERSON_C]’s claims had been previously adjudicated and that they were barred by the applicable statute of limitations. [PERSON_A] claimed that, while representing her, [PERSON_B] recklessly failed to raise that [PERSON_C]’s action was time-barred and recklessly failed to take [PERSON_C]’s deposition, which would have shown that the action was time-barred. [PERSON_A] claimed that [PERSON_B]’s failure to raise the issue timely caused increased attorney fees and costs and non-economic damages. [PERSON_B] argued that her failure to assert the statute-of-limitations defense in the earlier motions did not contribute to the judicial error because she had preserved that defense. [PERSON_A] claimed that if [PERSON_B] had asserted the statute-of-limitations defense timely and with supporting evidence, [PERSON_C]’s action would have been dismissed. [PERSON_A] claimed that [PERSON_B] negligently failed to argue that [PERSON_C]’s claims were barred by the statute of limitations. [PERSON_D] testified that [PERSON_B]’s omission from the initial motion caused [PERSON_A] financial and emotional harm.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: In February 1993, [PERSON_A] attended a three-week class provided by [ORGANIZATION_A] in which he was instructed regarding how to climb a wooden utility pole using equipment designed for that purpose. At the end of the course, [PERSON_A] purchased from [ORGANIZATION_A] the equipment that he had used during the course. This equipment consisted of a body belt, gaffs, and a pole strap. Shortly after completing the three-week climbing course, [PERSON_A] was hired by [COMPANY_A] as an apprentice linesman. On April 3, 1993, [PERSON_A] was working on a utility pole. While descending the pole, he fell to the ground from a height of approximately 18.3 meters. [PERSON_A] received serious injuries from the fall. At the time of the fall, [PERSON_A] had disconnected his pole strap to maneuver around a \"cross bar\" extending from the pole. The climbing method taught by [ORGANIZATION_A] involved unhooking the pole strap from the \"D\" ring on the body belt, moving past the obstacle, and rehooking the strap around the pole. [PERSON_A] alleged that [ORGANIZATION_A] supplied inappropriate climbing equipment and failed to provide adequate instructions, education, and warnings regarding pole climbing. [PERSON_A] testified that the manner in which he attempted to negotiate the obstacle was the only method taught to him by [ORGANIZATION_A]. [ORGANIZATION_A] argued that it had no responsibility to instruct [PERSON_A] to use fall arrest equipment. [PERSON_A] alleged that, while descending the utility pole with the equipment in the manner prescribed by [ORGANIZATION_A], he was injured while descending around the cross-arms, and that he would not have fallen but for [ORGANIZATION_A]'s improper instructions. [PERSON_A]'s expert testified that [PERSON_A] should have been instructed to use a second pole strap and that the second strap would have prevented the accident.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: 1993년 2월, [PERSON_A]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 제공한 3주 수업에 참석했으며, 그 수업에서 해당 목적을 위해 설계된 장비를 사용하여 목재 전신주를 오르는 방법에 관한 교육을 받았다. 과정이 끝날 때 [PERSON_A]는 과정 중 사용했던 장비를 [ORGANIZATION_A]로부터 구입했다. 이 장비는 안전벨트, 가프 및 전주 스트랩으로 구성되어 있었다. 3주간의 등반 과정을 마친 직후, [PERSON_A]는 [COMPANY_A]에 견습 전선공으로 고용되었다. 1993년 4월 3일, [PERSON_A]는 전신주에서 작업하고 있었다. 전신주를 내려오던 중 그는 약 18.3미터 높이에서 지면으로 추락했다. [PERSON_A]는 추락으로 중상을 입었다. 추락 당시 [PERSON_A]는 전신주에서 뻗어 나온 \"크로스 바\"를 돌아 이동하기 위해 전주 스트랩을 분리한 상태였다. [ORGANIZATION_A]가 가르친 등반 방법은 안전벨트의 \"D\" 링에서 전주 스트랩의 고리를 풀고, 장애물을 지나 이동한 다음, 전신주 주위에 스트랩을 다시 거는 것이었다. [PERSON_A]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 부적절한 등반 장비를 제공했고 전신주 등반에 관한 적절한 지시, 교육 및 경고를 제공하지 않았다고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]는 자신이 장애물을 통과하려고 시도한 방식이 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 자신에게 가르친 유일한 방법이었다고 증언했다. [ORGANIZATION_A]는 [PERSON_A]에게 추락 방지 장비를 사용하도록 지시할 책임이 없다고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 정한 방식으로 장비를 착용하고 전신주를 내려오던 중 크로스암 주위를 내려오다가 부상을 입었으며, [ORGANIZATION_A]의 부적절한 지시가 없었다면 추락하지 않았을 것이라고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]의 전문가는 [PERSON_A]에게 두 번째 전주 스트랩을 사용하도록 지시했어야 하며, 두 번째 스트랩이 사고를 방지했을 것이라고 증언했다.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: In December 1999, [PERSON_A] suffered a fatal accident while driving an off-highway dump truck within the scope of his employment with [COMPANY_A], the general contractor on a construction site owned by [ORGANIZATION_A]. On the afternoon of December 1, 1999, [COMPANY_A] asked [PERSON_A], who usually drove water trucks on the site, to drive a loaded, heavy-duty, off-highway dump truck up a hill on a haul road, even though he had never driven that type of truck on this worksite. Testimony indicated that [PERSON_A] was apprehensive about driving that type of truck but accepted the assignment. [COMPANY_A] constructed temporary unpaved haul roads to transport materials between sections of the project. Testimony indicated that [COMPANY_B] inspectors had authority to act regarding safety violations on haul roads and could stop work if they perceived a dangerous condition. [COMPANY_A] had no contractual relationship with [COMPANY_B], and its contract with [ORGANIZATION_A] assigned [COMPANY_A] responsibility for the safety of its employees on site. [COMPANY_B] contended that [PERSON_A] drove off the road to avoid an oncoming grader despite having sufficient room to pass. [PERSON_B] asserted that the haul road collapsed because instability in the hill caused by coal seams. [PERSON_B] alleged that the haul road should have had flaggers, barricades, or radio contact for truck drivers. She also alleged that [COMPANY_B] failed to require proper construction and maintenance of the haul road and failed to inspect it. [COMPANY_B]'s safety monitor was to represent [ORGANIZATION_A] in construction-safety matters, review and approve contractor emergency procedures and site-safety plans, interview applicants for contractors' safety representatives, monitor those representatives' performance, and monitor contractors' compliance with applicable safety regulations at all work operations on a frequent and regular schedule. [PERSON_A] suffered fatal injuries when the truck plunged down an 8.5-meter embankment and landed upside down in 1.2 meters of water. [COMPANY_B] asserted that [PERSON_A]'s death resulted from the construction and maintenance of the haul road by [COMPANY_A]. An expert stated that [COMPANY_B]'s representative traveled on haul roads but did not notice steep grades, narrow width, faulty slope configuration, inadequate drainage, or the absence of a safety berm, and did not address hazardous weather conditions on the day of the accident despite concerns expressed by employees.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: 1999년 12월, [PERSON_A]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 소유한 건설 현장의 종합계약자인 [COMPANY_A]에 고용되어 업무를 수행하던 중 비도로용 덤프트럭을 운전하다 치명적인 사고를 당했다. 1999년 12월 1일 오후, 현장에서 보통 물 운반 트럭을 운전하던 [PERSON_A]에게 [COMPANY_A]는 적재된 대형 비도로용 덤프트럭을 운반도로를 따라 언덕 위로 운전하라고 요청했다. [PERSON_A]는 이 작업 현장에서 그 유형의 트럭을 운전해 본 적이 없었다. 증언에 따르면 [PERSON_A]는 그러한 유형의 트럭을 운전하는 것을 불안해했지만 그 업무를 받아들였다. [COMPANY_A]는 프로젝트의 구역들 사이에서 자재를 운반하기 위해 임시 비포장 운반도로를 건설했다. 증언에 따르면 [COMPANY_B]의 검사관들은 운반도로의 안전 위반에 관해 조치할 권한이 있었고, 위험한 상태라고 판단하면 작업을 중단시킬 수 있었다. [COMPANY_A]는 [COMPANY_B]와 계약 관계가 없었고, [ORGANIZATION_A]와의 계약에 따라 현장 직원들의 안전에 대한 책임을 [COMPANY_A]가 부담하도록 되어 있었다. [COMPANY_B]는 [PERSON_A]가 지나갈 충분한 공간이 있었음에도 마주 오던 그레이더를 피하기 위해 도로 밖으로 운전했다고 주장했다. [PERSON_B]는 탄층으로 인해 발생한 언덕의 불안정성 때문에 운반도로가 붕괴했다고 주장했다. [PERSON_B]는 운반도로에 신호수, 바리케이드 또는 트럭 운전자들을 위한 무선 연락이 있어야 했다고 주장했다. 또한 [COMPANY_B]가 운반도로의 적절한 건설과 유지관리를 요구하지 않았고 이를 검사하지도 않았다고 주장했다. [COMPANY_B]의 안전 담당자는 건설 안전 문제에서 [ORGANIZATION_A]를 대표하고, 계약자의 비상 절차와 현장 안전 계획을 검토하고 승인하며, 계약자의 안전 대표자 지원자들을 면접하고, 해당 대표자들의 업무 수행을 감독하며, 모든 작업에서 계약자들이 적용 가능한 안전 규정을 준수하는지를 빈번하고 정기적으로 감독하도록 되어 있었다. 트럭이 8.5미터 높이의 둑 아래로 곤두박질쳐 1.2미터 깊이의 물속에 거꾸로 떨어지면서 [PERSON_A]는 치명적인 부상을 입었다. [COMPANY_B]는 [PERSON_A]의 사망이 [COMPANY_A]의 운반도로 건설 및 유지관리로 인해 발생했다고 주장했다. 한 전문가는 [COMPANY_B]의 대표자가 운반도로를 이동했지만 급한 경사, 좁은 폭, 잘못된 경사면 형상, 불충분한 배수 또는 안전 둑의 부재를 알아차리지 못했고, 직원들이 우려를 표명했음에도 사고 당일의 위험한 기상 상태에 대처하지 않았다고 진술했다.
aligned_fact_units.source_text: In December 1999, [PERSON_A] suffered a fatal accident while driving an off-highway dump truck within the scope of his employment with [COMPANY_A], the general contractor on a construction site owned by [ORGANIZATION_A]. On the afternoon of December 1, 1999, [COMPANY_A] asked [PERSON_A], who usually drove water trucks on the site, to drive a loaded, heavy-duty, off-highway dump truck up a hill on a haul road, even though he had never driven that type of truck on this worksite. Testimony indicated that [PERSON_A] was apprehensive about driving that type of truck but accepted the assignment. [COMPANY_A] constructed temporary unpaved haul roads to transport materials between sections of the project. Testimony indicated that [COMPANY_B] inspectors had authority to act regarding safety violations on haul roads and could stop work if they perceived a dangerous condition. [COMPANY_A] had no contractual relationship with [COMPANY_B], and its contract with [ORGANIZATION_A] assigned [COMPANY_A] responsibility for the safety of its employees on site. [COMPANY_B] contended that [PERSON_A] drove off the road to avoid an oncoming grader despite having sufficient room to pass. [PERSON_B] asserted that the haul road collapsed because instability in the hill caused by coal seams. [PERSON_B] alleged that the haul road should have had flaggers, barricades, or radio contact for truck drivers. She also alleged that [COMPANY_B] failed to require proper construction and maintenance of the haul road and failed to inspect it. [COMPANY_B]'s safety monitor was to represent [ORGANIZATION_A] in construction-safety matters, review and approve contractor emergency procedures and site-safety plans, interview applicants for contractors' safety representatives, monitor those representatives' performance, and monitor contractors' compliance with applicable safety regulations at all work operations on a frequent and regular schedule. [PERSON_A] suffered fatal injuries when the truck plunged down an 8.5-meter embankment and landed upside down in 1.2 meters of water. [COMPANY_B] asserted that [PERSON_A]'s death resulted from the construction and maintenance of the haul road by [COMPANY_A]. An expert stated that [COMPANY_B]'s representative traveled on haul roads but did not notice steep grades, narrow width, faulty slope configuration, inadequate drainage, or the absence of a safety berm, and did not address hazardous weather conditions on the day of the accident despite concerns expressed by employees.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] were dairy farmers during the 1970s and 1980s. In 1986, they sold their dairy cows in a government buyout program. In 1993, they bought a new herd and resumed dairy farming. Shortly after buying the new herd, they concluded that their earlier milk-production problems were caused by stray voltage. Stray voltage, also referred to as neutral-to-earth voltage, can affect livestock and cause decreased milk production in dairy cows. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] alleged that stray voltage depressed milk production on their farm until the neutrals were separated, after which milk production returned to normal. Stray voltage on a farm may be caused by a problem on the farm, a problem in [COMPANY_A]'s off-farm wires, or a problem on another customer's property, such as a neighboring farm.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]는 1970년대와 1980년대에 낙농업자였다. 1986년에 그들은 정부의 매입 프로그램을 통해 젖소를 팔았다. 1993년에 그들은 새 가축 떼를 사서 낙농업을 재개했다. 새 가축 떼를 산 직후, 그들은 이전의 우유 생산 문제가 누설 전압으로 인해 발생했다고 결론지었다. 중성선-대지 전압이라고도 하는 누설 전압은 가축에 영향을 미치고 젖소의 우유 생산량 감소를 초래할 수 있다. [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]는 중성선들이 분리될 때까지 누설 전압이 자신들의 농장에서 우유 생산량을 감소시켰고, 그 후 우유 생산량이 정상으로 돌아왔다고 주장했다. 농장의 누설 전압은 농장 내 문제, [COMPANY_A]의 농장 외부 전선 문제, 또는 이웃 농장과 같은 다른 고객의 부지에 있는 문제로 인해 발생할 수 있다.

source_fact_units.model_source_span: Since 1860, this Court has relied on the Taking Clause to support actions for trespass-nuisance. This Court has held many times that an invasion by government-controlled waters or sewage creates a cause of action against which governmental immunity is not a bar.[10] On the basis of that long-established precedent, I would hold that a trespass-nuisance cause of action is constitutionally based and cannot be abrogated by the Legislature. The actions of the defendants here in flooding the plaintiffs' basements constitute a "taking," and damages, if proven, should be available. The basis for recovery is that the government deprived plaintiffs of the useful possession of property that they own.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [PERSON_B] was driving [VEHICLE_B] when [PERSON_A]’s rented [VEHICLE_A] collided with it; [PERSON_B] died, and her children [PERSON_C] and [PERSON_D] and their friend [PERSON_E] were injured. [PERSON_A] later stated that he had been given [VEHICLE_C] with instructions to drive to [LOCATION_A] and pick up six people from a parking lot, and that he had been paid to make the trip. By March 21, [PERSON_A] had made one out-and-back trip to [LOCATION_A]. Around noon on March 21, [PERSON_A] brought [VEHICLE_C] to a branch of [COMPANY_A] after it had been driven approximately 12,392 kilometers since [PERSON_F] rented it on March 13; [PERSON_A] reported a bad transmission and requested another vehicle. [PERSON_G], a branch manager for [COMPANY_A], checked the company’s internal computer system, saw [PERSON_A] listed as an additional driver, viewed his unexpired driver’s license, and later attested that [PERSON_A] did not appear impaired, intoxicated, or otherwise unfit to drive. [PERSON_A] attested that he gave [COMPANY_A] personnel no reason to believe that he was under the influence of drugs or alcohol or incapable of driving; [PERSON_G] accepted [VEHICLE_C], provided [VEHICLE_A] to [PERSON_A], and watched him drive away. [PERSON_A] later stated that he ingested cocaine overnight and “rested but he didn’t sleep.” [PERSON_A] stated that he told [PERSON_F] he was tired and that [PERSON_F] told him to continue driving; roughly twenty-four hours after obtaining [VEHICLE_A], [PERSON_A] drove it northward in a southbound lane while [PERSON_B] drove [VEHICLE_B] southward in that lane, and the vehicles collided. The collision killed [PERSON_B], seriously injured [PERSON_C], [PERSON_D], and [PERSON_E], and caused minor injuries to [PERSON_A]. [COMPANY_B] insured supplemental coverage, [COMPANY_C] investigated the collision, and a claims supervisor first denied coverage because [PERSON_A] was not listed as an authorized driver before rescinding that disclaimer and reserving coverage rights.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: In April 1999, [PERSON_A] purchased a spray bottle of [PRODUCT_A] from [COMPANY_A]. [COMPANY_C], later acquired by [COMPANY_D], packaged and labeled [PRODUCT_A], a spray-on body and hair moisturizer containing eight natural oils. The label warned users not to spray the product near sparks or an open flame, but it did not state that the product could be harmful or fatal if swallowed or that it should be kept out of reach of children. [PERSON_A]'s 11-month-old son, [PERSON_B], was left unattended and obtained the bottle, which had been within his reach. He put an unknown amount of the product into his mouth, and some entered his lungs. He was admitted to a hospital with hydrocarbon ingestion and chemical pneumonitis and died about one month later from multisystem organ failure associated with chemical pneumonitis after hydrocarbon ingestion. [PERSON_A] stated that the bottle had been intact when she last used it earlier that day; when she later saw [PERSON_B] with the bottle, the plastic top and pump actuator were missing, and the plastic base of the pump actuator was cracked. [PERSON_A] also stated that she generally read product labels because she had two small children and kept products she knew to be toxic in locked storage.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: 1999년 4월 [PERSON_A]는 [COMPANY_A]에서 [PRODUCT_A] 스프레이 한 병을 구입했다. 이후 [COMPANY_D]에 인수된 [COMPANY_C]는 8가지 천연 오일을 함유한 분사형 신체·모발 보습제인 [PRODUCT_A]를 포장하고 라벨을 부착했다. 라벨에는 불꽃이나 화염 근처에서 제품을 분사하지 말라는 경고가 있었지만, 제품을 삼킬 경우 유해하거나 치명적일 수 있다는 내용이나 어린이의 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 보관하라는 내용은 없었다. [PERSON_A]의 11개월 된 아들 [PERSON_B]는 보호자 없이 있던 중 손이 닿는 곳에 있던 제품 병을 손에 넣었다. [PERSON_B]는 알 수 없는 양의 제품을 입에 넣었고 일부가 폐로 들어갔다. [PERSON_B]는 탄화수소 섭취와 화학성 폐렴으로 병원에 입원했고, 약 한 달 뒤 탄화수소 섭취에 따른 화학성 폐렴과 관련된 다기관 장기부전으로 사망했다. [PERSON_A]는 그날 앞서 제품을 마지막으로 사용했을 때 병이 온전했다고 진술했으나, 나중에 [PERSON_B]가 병을 들고 있는 것을 보았을 때 플라스틱 상단과 펌프 작동기가 없어져 있었고 펌프 작동기의 플라스틱 바닥 부분이 갈라져 있었다고 진술했다. [PERSON_A]는 어린 자녀가 둘 있어 일반적으로 제품 라벨을 읽었고, 유독하다고 알고 있는 제품은 잠금장치가 있는 곳에 보관했다고 진술했다.

[PERSON_B]가 두 번째로 구토한 후 약 20~30분 뒤, [PERSON_C]는 상시 지시에 따라 의사에게 전화했다. [PERSON_C]가 의사와 연락할 수 없자 그는 자신의 상급자에게 알린 후 30분간 휴식을 취했다. [PERSON_B]의 딸인 [PERSON_A]는 하루 종일 그와 연락하고 있었다. [PERSON_A]는 누군가를 [PERSON_B]의 방으로 보내 달라고 시도했으나 실패한 후, 오후 약 6시 45분에 [ORGANIZATION_A]로 가서 [PERSON_B]가 심하게 떨며 호흡 곤란을 겪고 있는 것을 발견했다. The bus carrying [PERSON_C] and [PERSON_D] stopped, and they were forced to exit it and saw [PERSON_B]'s injured body. The petition alleged that no teachers were on duty in or around the bus area of [ORGANIZATION_A] when the accident occurred. The petition alleged that [ORGANIZATION_D] personnel failed to supervise the children, failed to respond to the fight promptly, and failed to staff the bus area adequately with teachers or other school employees. The petition alleged that [PERSON_G] saw or should have seen the large student gathering and the fight between [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_E], yet continued operating the bus near the crowd without regard for the children's safety. The petition alleged that [PERSON_F]'s role in inciting the fight and [PERSON_E]'s alleged push of [PERSON_B], which allegedly caused her to fall, contributed to the resulting harm. The petition alleged that [COMPANY_A] issued [ORGANIZATION_D] a liability insurance policy covering [PERSON_G]'s alleged negligent acts.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: In February 1992, [PERSON_A] was 42 years old, had worked as a registered nurse for about 20 years, and owned a small business and a home with her husband. [PERSON_A] wanted to prepare for retirement, and her husband arranged a meeting between her and [PERSON_B], a sales representative of [COMPANY_A], to discuss a product offered by [COMPANY_A]. According to [PERSON_A]'s deposition testimony, [PERSON_B] presented [PRODUCT_A] as a savings vehicle that could generate approximately [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A] at age 65 through monthly payments of [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A], and said that life insurance was part of the plan. After [PERSON_A] expressed interest, [PERSON_B] had her complete and sign an application for life insurance; the following month, [PERSON_A] received [PRODUCT_B] from [COMPANY_A]. [PRODUCT_B] was identified as a whole life policy with a face amount of [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A], life insurance payable at the insured's death, premiums payable for a stated period, and annual dividends. [PRODUCT_B] stated a guaranteed cash value at age 65 of [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A] based on a 4% annual guaranteed interest rate. [PERSON_A] looked only at [PRODUCT_B]'s cover sheet, paid [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A] in premiums to [COMPANY_A], stopped making payments in 1994 after becoming concerned that she had purchased life insurance, and [PRODUCT_B] lapsed. [PERSON_A] alleged that [COMPANY_A] and [PERSON_B] marketed [PRODUCT_B] as a savings or investment vehicle rather than as life insurance. [PERSON_A] alleged that she purchased unwanted life insurance and did not obtain the retirement product she needed. [PERSON_A] alleged that [COMPANY_A] and [PERSON_B]'s misrepresentations caused her to purchase unwanted life insurance and prevented her from obtaining the retirement product she needed. [PERSON_A] asserted that [PERSON_B] told her that the [COMPANY_A] product she was purchasing included a life insurance component.

neutral_fact_en: [COMPANY_A] operated a timber-removal business, and [PERSON_A] was employed by [COMPANY_A] as a timber cutter. [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C] were [PERSON_A]’s parents and co-administrators of his estate. aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [ORGANIZATION_A] hired [COMPANY_A], a general contractor, to construct improvements to [LOCATION_A]. After construction was completed, [COMPANY_B] filed a complaint against [COMPANY_A] for unpaid amounts due on its completed work. [COMPANY_A] brought a third-party complaint against [ORGANIZATION_A] concerning indemnity, contribution, and wrongful interference with a prospective business advantage. [COMPANY_A]'s expert prepared a report on delay damages allegedly caused by [ORGANIZATION_A]. [COMPANY_A] alleged that [ORGANIZATION_A]'s failure to produce documents needed to complete the report caused the expert's report to be late. During [PERSON_A]'s testimony at trial, he disclosed that he possessed a file that he had not produced to the parties' attorneys. The following day, [PERSON_A] produced the file, which contained nearly 1,700 documents. According to [PERSON_A], he told [PERSON_B] that he would not sign the affidavit because he had located another file but had not yet reviewed it. According to [PERSON_A], [PERSON_B] told him not to look in the file. [PERSON_B], however, testified that he never instructed [PERSON_A] not to look at any files. This dispute resulted in nearly a one-week delay in the trial. [PERSON_A] turned over approximately 1,700 documents to the court, 500 to 700 of which had not been previously produced. [ORGANIZATION_A]'s counsel sought to question [PERSON_C] about whether [COMPANY_A]'s subcontractors may have caused [COMPANY_A]'s delays, which led to [COMPANY_A]'s damages. [PERSON_C] testified that [COMPANY_A]'s contract stated the number of days it would need to complete the project, which implied that [COMPANY_A] was at fault for not completing the project on time. The architectural department head testified that determining whether the delays resulted from [ORGANIZATION_A]'s poor design would require reviewing the project plans, which [COMPANY_A] did not offer into evidence. The record indicates that [ORGANIZATION_A] performed under the contract.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: [ORGANIZATION_A]는 [LOCATION_A]에 개선 공사를 수행하도록 종합건설업자인 [COMPANY_A]를 고용했다. 공사가 완료된 후, [COMPANY_B]는 자신이 완료한 작업에 대해 지급되지 않은 금액을 청구하며 [COMPANY_A]를 상대로 청구를 제기했다. [COMPANY_A]는 보상, 분담 및 장래의 사업상 이익에 대한 부당한 방해와 관련하여 [ORGANIZATION_A]를 상대로 제3자 청구를 제기했다. [COMPANY_A]의 전문가는 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 야기했다고 주장된 지연 손해에 관한 보고서를 작성했다. [COMPANY_A]는 보고서 완성에 필요한 문서를 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 제출하지 않아 전문가의 보고서가 늦어졌다고 주장했다. 재판에서 [PERSON_A]가 증언하는 동안, 그는 당사자들의 변호사들에게 제출하지 않은 파일을 자신이 가지고 있다고 밝혔다. 다음 날, [PERSON_A]는 그 파일을 제출했으며, 그 파일에는 거의 1,700개의 문서가 들어 있었다. [PERSON_A]에 따르면, 그는 다른 파일을 찾았지만 아직 검토하지 않았기 때문에 진술서에 서명하지 않겠다고 [PERSON_B]에게 말했다. [PERSON_A]에 따르면, [PERSON_B]는 그에게 파일을 살펴보지 말라고 말했다. 그러나 [PERSON_B]는 자신이 [PERSON_A]에게 어떤 파일도 살펴보지 말라고 지시한 적이 없다고 증언했다. 이 분쟁으로 인해 재판이 거의 1주일 지연되었다. [PERSON_A]는 약 1,700개의 문서를 법원에 제출했으며, 그중 500개에서 700개는 이전에 제출되지 않았던 문서였다. [ORGANIZATION_A]의 변호사는 [COMPANY_A]의 하도급업체들이 [COMPANY_A]의 지연을 야기했을 가능성이 있는지, 그리고 그 지연이 [COMPANY_A]의 손해로 이어졌는지에 관해 [PERSON_C]를 신문하려 했다. [PERSON_C]는 [COMPANY_A]의 계약서에 해당 프로젝트를 완료하는 데 필요한 일수가 명시되어 있었으며, 이는 [COMPANY_A]가 프로젝트를 제때 완료하지 못한 데 책임이 있음을 시사한다고 증언했다. 건축 부서 책임자는 지연이 [ORGANIZATION_A]의 부실한 설계로 인해 발생했는지를 판단하려면 프로젝트 도면을 검토해야 하며, [COMPANY_A]는 그 도면을 증거로 제출하지 않았다고 증언했다. 기록에 따르면 [ORGANIZATION_A]는 계약에 따라 이행했다.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] were spouses. [PERSON_A] ate several [PRODUCT_A] that [COMPANY_A] designed, manufactured, and sold. After eating the [PRODUCT_A], [PERSON_A] felt as though chips had lodged in his throat and sought emergency hospital care. Medical procedures showed that [PERSON_A] suffered an esophageal tear resulting in serious physical injuries. The [PRODUCT_A] that [PERSON_A] had eaten allegedly caused the esophageal tear. [PERSON_C] opined that [COMPANY_A] failed to warn about the dangers of eating [PRODUCT_A]. [PERSON_C] tested the compressive strength of dry [PRODUCT_A] by pressing each chip's triangular tip onto a padded platform scale until the chip snapped. [PERSON_C] tested how long saliva took to soften [PRODUCT_A] by holding chips in his mouth for 15, 30, 45, and 60 seconds. [PERSON_C] opined that the uneven and dangerous characteristics of [PRODUCT_A] caused [PERSON_A]'s esophageal tear and resulting injuries. [PERSON_D] opined that the [PRODUCT_A] [PERSON_A] ate lacerated his esophagus while passing to his stomach and that the laceration caused [PERSON_A]'s injuries. [COMPANY_A] alleged that [PERSON_A] had not produced sufficient evidence that [PRODUCT_A] had a defect, was improperly designed or manufactured, or caused [PERSON_A]'s esophagus to tear, and that expert testimony was necessary to prove those matters. [COMPANY_A]'s expert, Martin R. Okos, questioned the validity of [PERSON_C]'s tests and the accuracy of his results.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]는 배우자였다. [PERSON_A]는 [COMPANY_A]가 설계하고 제조하여 판매한 [PRODUCT_A]를 여러 개 먹었다. [PRODUCT_A]를 먹은 후, [PERSON_A]는 칩이 목에 걸린 것처럼 느꼈고 응급 병원 진료를 받으러 갔다. 의료 절차를 통해 [PERSON_A]가 식도 파열을 겪었고 그 결과 심각한 신체적 부상을 입었다는 사실이 나타났다. [PERSON_A]가 먹은 [PRODUCT_A]가 식도 파열을 일으켰다고 주장되었다. aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [PERSON_A] is the child of [PERSON_B], and [COMPANY_A], [COMPANY_B], [COMPANY_C], [PERSON_C], and [PERSON_D] were involved in the events surrounding [PERSON_A]’s birth. [PERSON_B] received prenatal care from [COMPANY_C], whose obstetricians included [PERSON_C] and [PERSON_D]. [PERSON_B] was primarily attended by [PERSON_C] during [PERSON_A]’s delivery. [PERSON_B]’s amniotic and chorionic membranes ruptured at approximately 5:30 a.m. on July 16, 1980, and she was admitted to [COMPANY_A] within 30 minutes. A resident doctor noted that [PERSON_A]’s fetal heart tones were within a normal range. [PERSON_C] gave a single order for Pitocin that, according to [PERSON_G]’s testimony, was filled twice: once through the 5% Ringer’s lactate solution and once through a D5W solution. Medical records indicated that [PERSON_B] inadvertently received two doses of Pitocin, with the first administered shortly after 11:00 a.m. on [PERSON_C]’s order. [PERSON_A] has cerebral palsy, mental retardation, and other neurological and physical ailments. [PERSON_G] testified that excessive and severe contractions reduced the flow of oxygenated blood to [PERSON_A] by compressing the umbilical cord and reducing oxygenation periods between contractions, resulting in hypoxia and related heart-rate decelerations. According to [PERSON_H]’s testimony, [PERSON_A] suffered trauma when successive, high-pressure uterine contractions pounded or ground his head into the pelvic rim, causing marked heart-rate decelerations; [PERSON_H] also testified that the described events would not have occurred without Pitocin.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: [PERSON_A]는 [PERSON_B]의 자녀이며, [COMPANY_A], [COMPANY_B], [COMPANY_C], [PERSON_C], 및 [PERSON_D]는 [PERSON_A]의 출생을 둘러싼 사건에 관여했다. [PERSON_B]는 [COMPANY_C]에서 산전 관리를 받았으며, 그곳의 산과 의사에는 [PERSON_C]와 [PERSON_D]가 포함되어 있었다. [PERSON_A]의 분만 중에는 주로 [PERSON_C]가 [PERSON_B]를 진료했다. [PERSON_B]의 양막과 융모막은 1980년 7월 16일 오전 5시 30분경 파열되었고, [PERSON_B]는 30분 이내에 [COMPANY_A]에 입원했다. 레지던트 의사는 [PERSON_A]의 태아 심박음이 정상 범위 내에 있었다고 기록했다. [PERSON_C]는 피토신을 한 번만 처방했으나, [PERSON_G]의 증언에 따르면 그 처방은 두 번 조제되었다. 한 번은 5% 링거 젖산 용액을 통해, 또 한 번은 D5W 용액을 통해 조제되었다. 의료 기록에는 [PERSON_B]가 의도하지 않게 피토신을 두 차례 투여받았으며, 첫 번째 투여는 [PERSON_C]의 처방에 따라 오전 11시 직후에 이루어졌다고 기재되어 있었다. [PERSON_A]는 뇌성마비, 정신지체 및 기타 신경학적·신체적 질환을 앓고 있다. [PERSON_G]는 과도하고 심한 수축이 탯줄을 압박하고 수축 사이의 산소 공급 기간을 줄여 [PERSON_A]에게 산소가 공급된 혈액의 흐름을 감소시켰으며, 그 결과 저산소증과 이에 따른 심박수 감속이 발생했다고 증언했다. [PERSON_H]의 증언에 따르면, 연속적인 고압 자궁 수축이 [PERSON_A]의 머리를 골반 가장자리에 두드리거나 짓눌러 현저한 심박수 감속을 일으켰을 때 [PERSON_A]는 외상을 입었다고 한다. [PERSON_H]는 또한 피토신이 없었다면 기술된 사건들은 발생하지 않았을 것이라고 증언했다.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: Before 1997, [COMPANY_A], a corporation with its principal place of business in [LOCATION_A], owned all of the stock of three health maintenance organizations. After the transfer of funds, none of the three HMOs again met the applicable regulatory or statutory financial requirements. After the sale, the transfer of [COMPANY_B]’s reserves for future health care costs was followed by cash-flow difficulties at the three HMOs, which were still losing money. [PERSON_A] warned [COMPANY_B]’s representative and other recipients that regulators were increasingly concerned about the large intercompany payables recorded by the HMOs, and later requested an immediate infusion of cash and capital to continue operations.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [PERSON_A] was a nine-year-old student at [ORGANIZATION_A] when he participated in a relay race during gym class. During the relay race, [PERSON_A] tripped and fell into the concrete wall at the end of the gym. The gym wall had no padding and was made of concrete. The impact caused [PERSON_A] to hit and cut his head and lose consciousness; he was later diagnosed with a concussion, missed school for one to two months, and continued to experience headaches and memory problems years later. [PERSON_A]’s fall propelled him into the unpadded concrete wall, which caused the head impact and resulting loss of consciousness. [PERSON_B] alleged that [ORGANIZATION_A] and [ORGANIZATION_B] failed to install padded safety mats to cushion the concrete gym wall. [PERSON_B] alleged that [PERSON_A]’s injuries were caused by the defective and dangerous condition of the gym wall resulting from [ORGANIZATION_A] and [ORGANIZATION_B]’s alleged failure to install safety mats. [ORGANIZATION_B] alleged that the wall had no defect or condition that caused [PERSON_A]’s injury and that the injury instead resulted from a teacher directing students to run toward the wall and from [PERSON_A] tripping and falling. [PERSON_A] testified that he was injured because he was running too fast, tripped, and fell.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: [PERSON_A]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]의 9세 학생으로 체육 수업 중 이어달리기 경주에 참가했다. 이어달리기 경주 중 [PERSON_A]는 발을 헛디뎌 체육관 끝의 콘크리트 벽에 부딪혀 넘어졌다. 체육관 벽에는 완충재가 없었고 콘크리트로 되어 있었다. 충격으로 [PERSON_A]는 머리를 부딪혀 머리에 상처를 입고 의식을 잃었으며, 이후 뇌진탕 진단을 받고 1~2개월 동안 학교에 결석했고, 수년 후에도 계속 두통과 기억력 문제를 겪었다. [PERSON_A]가 넘어지면서 완충재가 없는 콘크리트 벽으로 튕겨 나갔고, 그로 인해 머리를 부딪히고 그 결과 의식을 잃었다. [PERSON_B]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]와 [ORGANIZATION_B]가 체육관 콘크리트 벽의 충격을 완화할 완충 안전 매트를 설치하지 않았다고 주장했다. [PERSON_B]는 [PERSON_A]의 부상이 [ORGANIZATION_A]와 [ORGANIZATION_B]가 안전 매트를 설치하지 않았다는 주장된 불이행으로 인해 발생한 체육관 벽의 결함 있고 위험한 상태 때문에 발생했다고 주장했다. [ORGANIZATION_B]는 벽에 [PERSON_A]의 부상을 초래한 결함이나 상태가 없었으며, 오히려 그 부상은 교사가 학생들에게 벽을 향해 달리라고 지시한 것과 [PERSON_A]가 발을 헛디뎌 넘어짐으로 인해 발생했다고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]는 자신이 너무 빨리 달리다가 발을 헛디뎌 넘어져 부상을 입었다고 증언했다.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: In 1995, [PERSON_C], a financial advisor for [COMPANY_A], initiated an unsolicited telephone contact with [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] and asked to meet regarding their finances. [PERSON_A] told [PERSON_C] that he had a long-term disability policy, and [PERSON_C] reviewed the policy at a later meeting and advised them to keep it because he could not offer a comparable product. In December 1995, for a fee, [PERSON_C] presented [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] with a financial management proposal that identified him as their financial advisor and stated that, at their request, he could recommend products distributed by [COMPANY_D] and its affiliates as alternatives for existing securities. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] provided [PERSON_C] with information about their existing policies with [COMPANY_B]. [PERSON_C] proposed one [PRODUCT_A] in January 1996 and another in June 1996. The June proposal included coverage for [PERSON_A] and a rider for [PERSON_B]. [PERSON_A] purchased that policy and cashed out his five existing policies to make the initial payment. In 1997, [PERSON_B] used proceeds from her two policies with [COMPANY_B] to purchase a [PRODUCT_B]. In 1998, [PERSON_C] proposed increasing [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B]'s life insurance coverage, but they rejected the proposal because they decided that they had enough coverage. In 2000, they had their portfolio independently reviewed. The independent review informed [PERSON_A] that the 1996 [PRODUCT_A] was underfunded and expected to lapse, requiring additional premiums at substantially high rates that would increase over time. The review also informed [PERSON_B] that the 1997 [PRODUCT_B] would not mature until she was eighty-four rather than sixty-five, as had allegedly been represented by [PERSON_C]. The review linked the underfunding of the 1996 [PRODUCT_A] with its expected lapse and the need for additional premiums at rates increasing over time. The policy illustration presented separate current and guaranteed interest-rate columns and stated that there would be no surrender value at age eighty-two. [PERSON_A] signed a disclosure stating that current interest rates were not a prediction of future policy performance. [PERSON_A] testified that [PERSON_C] represented that the monthly premiums would be [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A] for eight years, after which the policy would be paid off. [PERSON_B] testified that they often signed documents based on [PERSON_C]'s representations about their contents and that she treated him as her advisor and relied on his word. [PERSON_A] testified that they trusted [PERSON_C] because they believed he knew what was best. [PERSON_A] testified that he had graduated from high school; [PERSON_B]'s educational background was not stated in her testimony. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] allege that [COMPANY_C] and [PERSON_C] presented themselves as experts in financial and retirement planning, while they had only high school educations and no experience working with a financial advisor. They allege that they reasonably believed and trusted that [PERSON_C] prepared the proposal and recommended the 1996 [PRODUCT_A] with their best interests in mind. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] accepted [PERSON_C]'s advice regarding the purchase of the 1996 [PRODUCT_A] and made the decision to purchase it. They also rejected other products and services. [PERSON_B]는 그들이 문서의 내용에 관한 [PERSON_C]의 설명을 바탕으로 자주 문서에 서명했으며, 자신은 그를 자문가로 대하고 [PERSON_C]의 말을 신뢰했다고 증언했다. [PERSON_A]는 그들이 [PERSON_C]가 무엇이 최선인지 알고 있다고 믿었기 때문에 그를 신뢰했다고 증언했다. [PERSON_A]는 자신이 고등학교를 졸업했다고 증언했으며, [PERSON_B]의 교육 배경은 [PERSON_B]의 증언에서 언급되지 않았다. On appeal, they merely contend that, unlike the scenario in Rothman, here the ATO respondents ratified Clack's actions when the ATO-UNR officers suffered memory loss when giving their statements to the police.

The unavoidable danger that led to plaintiff’s injury was working at a dangerous height. The scaffold was the platform provided for the workers to walk on while working at a dangerous height, and there was fall-protection equipment available that plaintiff could have worn, but he did not do so.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [COMPANY_C] provided prenatal care to [PERSON_B] and employed four obstetricians, including [PERSON_C] and [PERSON_D]. At 10:00, [PERSON_B] began to receive 1 litre of a 5% Ringer's lactate solution through the "keep open" IV line. [PERSON_C], who had taken over for [PERSON_D] sometime after [PERSON_B] was admitted, met with [PERSON_B] at approximately 11:00 A.M. He was concerned that [PERSON_B] and her child had been exposed to infection since her membranes burst earlier that morning,[3] and concluded that [PERSON_B] should be given ten units of [MEDICATION_A] in order to induce labor.[5] From 11:30 A.M. to 6:00 P.M., [PERSON_B] was given doses of [MEDICATION_A] in increasing amounts. [PERSON_B]'s amniotic and chorionic membranes ruptured at approximately 5:30 A.M. on July 16, 1980, and she was admitted to [COMPANY_A] within a half hour. The resident doctor on call at the time noted that [PERSON_A]'s fetal heart tones were within a normal range. [PERSON_D], who was the attending physician on staff when [PERSON_B] was admitted, requested that [PERSON_B] be given an intravenous (IV) "keep open" line to maintain hydration and to establish a channel for the intravenous administration of medication, should the need arise. Nurses applied an [DEVICE_A] to [PERSON_B] at approximately 9:30 A.M., at which time she still had not experienced contractions. [PERSON_E] reported that [PERSON_B]'s medical records revealed that she was inadvertently given two doses of [MEDICATION_A]. [PERSON_B]'s records showed that she had administered [MEDICATION_A] through D5W,[6] a solution other than the 5% Ringer's lactate [PERSON_B] was already receiving intravenously. Thus, according to [PERSON_E]'s account, [PERSON_C] had given a single order for [MEDICATION_A] that had been filled twice  once by Nurse Quinlan through the 5% Ringer's lactate solution, and once by Nurse Tyra through the D5W solution. Medical records compiled after [PERSON_A]'s birth show that [PERSON_B] began experiencing contractions of "moderate" strength after receiving [MEDICATION_A] and that "moderate" contractions continued until [PERSON_A]'s delivery. [PERSON_A] experienced recurrent decelerations of his heart rate after [PERSON_B] began to receive [MEDICATION_A], according to [PERSON_E]'s interpretation of the fetal-monitor records; [PERSON_E] attributed the decelerations to contractions of excessive intensity and duration caused by [MEDICATION_A], and reported that the contractions compressed [PERSON_A]'s umbilical cord and decreased blood flow to him. The result was the pattern of decelerations in heart rate shown by the fetal uterine monitor and a decrease in the amount of oxygen flowing to [PERSON_A]'s brain, or "hypoxia" in medical parlance. [PERSON_A] was born shortly before 7:00 P.M. that day. His Apgar scores, 8 and 9 (on a one to ten scale), were well within the typical range,[7] indicating that [PERSON_A] appeared to be a normal, healthy baby. Two days after his birth, [PERSON_A] was examined by pediatrician [PERSON_H], who concluded that [PERSON_A] seemed to be healthy and displayed normal cognitive functions. [PERSON_A] received a vastly different diagnosis approximately one year later. [PERSON_B] had [PERSON_A] examined by [PERSON_G], a pediatric neurologist, after noticing that [PERSON_A] began to seem developmentally slow after his third month. [PERSON_G] diagnosed [PERSON_A] with nonprogressive encephalopathy[9] with global developmental delay and mild spasticity. He concluded at the time that the etiology or cause of [PERSON_A]'s condition was unclear.

[PERSON_B]의 기록에는 그녀가 D5W를 통해 [MEDICATION_A]를 투여했다고 되어 있었는데,[6] D5W는 [PERSON_B]가 이미 정맥으로 투여받고 있던 5% 링거 젖산 용액과는 다른 용액이었다. 따라서 [PERSON_E]의 설명에 따르면, [PERSON_C]는 [MEDICATION_A]에 대해 한 번의 처방을 내렸지만 그 처방은 두 번 조제되었다  한 번은 퀸런 간호사가 5% 링거 젖산 용액을 통해, 또 한 번은 타이라 간호사가 D5W 용액을 통해 조제했다. [PERSON_E]가 태아 모니터 기록을 해석한 바에 따르면, [PERSON_B]가 [MEDICATION_A]를 투여받기 시작한 후 [PERSON_A]는 심박수의 반복적인 감속을 겪었다. [PERSON_E]는 그 감속이 [MEDICATION_A]로 인해 발생한 과도한 강도와 지속시간의 수축 때문이라고 보았으며, 그 수축이 [PERSON_A]의 탯줄을 압박하여 그에게 흐르는 혈류를 감소시켰다고 보고했다. 그 결과는 태아 자궁 모니터에 나타난 심박수 감속 양상과 [PERSON_A]의 뇌로 흐르는 산소량의 감소, 즉 의학 용어로 "저산소증"이었다. [PERSON_A]는 그날 오후 7시 직전에 태어났다. [PERSON_A]의 아프가 점수는 8점과 9점(1점에서 10점까지의 척도)으로, 일반적인 범위 안에 충분히 들어갔으며,[7] 이는 [PERSON_A]가 정상적이고 건강한 아기로 보였음을 나타냈다. 출생 이틀 후 [PERSON_A]는 소아과 의사 [PERSON_H]의 진찰을 받았고, [PERSON_H]는 [PERSON_A]가 건강해 보이며 정상적인 인지 기능을 나타낸다고 결론 내렸다. 약 1년 후 [PERSON_A]는 매우 다른 진단을 받았다. [PERSON_B]는 [PERSON_A]가 생후 3개월이 지나면서 발달이 느린 것처럼 보이기 시작한 것을 알아차린 후, 소아 신경과 의사인 [PERSON_G]에게 [PERSON_A]를 검사받게 했다. [PERSON_G]는 [PERSON_A]를 전반적 발달 지연과 경도의 경직을 동반한 비진행성 뇌병증[9]으로 진단했다. 그는 당시 [PERSON_A]의 상태의 병인 또는 원인이 불분명하다고 결론 내렸다.

source_fact_units.model_source_span: We conclude that an expert affidavit is required for medical malpractice actions against professional medical corporations and professional negligence actions against nurses and nurse practitioners under NRS 41A.071, and therefore, we conclude that the district court did not err in dismissing the Fierles' complaint with regard to such claims. Additionally, we conclude that the district court erred in dismissing the negligent extravasation claim against one member of Dr. Perez's staff because that claim falls under the res ipsa loquitur statutory exception to NRS 41A.071 and, therefore, is not required to be supported by an expert medical affidavit. We further conclude that medical malpractice and professional negligence claims made in a complaint that become void ab initio for lack of the attachment of an expert affidavit may not be cured by the amendment of that complaint, regardless of whether other claims in the original complaint survive. FACTS In July 2005, Patricia was diagnosed with breast cancer. She then underwent a mastectomy. In addition to the mastectomy, a catheter was also surgically placed in Patricia's chest wall for the infusion of chemotherapy medications. In this procedure, the catheter is surgically attached to the tissue under the skin, and a second part of the catheter is placed into the subclavian vein.

source_fact_units.model_source_span: It is easy to imagine the trickle-down effect that a preservation policy would have on insureds themselves; the longer an insurer or auction company is required to store a vehicle, the higher the costs, and the more likely insurance premiums would be increased to absorb those costs. Moreover, the delay in proceeds being remitted to the insurer at the time of the auction prevents those funds from being immediately available to offset the total loss payout the insurer pays to the insured. Again, this practice could result in higher costs for the public.
