aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: In September 2007, [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] purchased a home from [PERSON_E] and [PERSON_F] and obtained a homeowner’s insurance policy for it from [COMPANY_A]. The policy covered [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] and their two minor children, [PERSON_C] and [PERSON_D], and included an endorsement covering physical loss to the property caused by mold. The rider obligated [COMPANY_A] to pay the Brunos up to [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A] for direct physical loss to the property caused by mold or necessary increased costs. The rider required [COMPANY_A] to pay for testing the air and covered property to determine the presence or level of mold and, if mold was present, to pay for its removal, including tearing out property needed to access it. On October 5, 2007, after [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] moved into the property, [PERSON_A], assisted by a contractor, began renovating the basement and removed part of the wood paneling covering the basement’s block walls. After the paneling was detached, [PERSON_A] discovered two areas of black mold on the block walls near leaking water pipes. [PERSON_A] informed [COMPANY_A] and said he wished to initiate a claim under the homeowner’s policy. [COMPANY_A] sent an adjuster to view the mold, and two days later the adjuster returned with an engineer employed by [COMPANY_B], which [COMPANY_A] had retained to investigate the mold, determine its severity, and assess the extent of remediation required. The adjuster refused payment, stating that he lacked authorization and that no coverage determination had been made. Based on the adjuster’s and engineer’s assurances that the mold was not a health hazard, [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] continued living in the property, and [PERSON_A] continued renovating it. During October, [PERSON_A] and a contractor attempted to eradicate the mold and removed additional paneling, revealing more leaking pipes and additional mold. [PERSON_A] informed [COMPANY_A] of the further discoveries. [COMPANY_A] sent the same engineer, who visually inspected the newly discovered mold and performed tests but did not disclose the results. During October, each family member began experiencing respiratory ailments that worsened over the following months. By January 2008, [PERSON_B] had developed severe coughing, difficulty breathing and clearing her throat, and intense headaches. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] then paid for mold testing, which revealed that the mold was toxic and hazardous to human health. In April 2008, [COMPANY_A] paid [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A] under the mold endorsement. [PERSON_B] was later diagnosed with throat and esophageal cancer, which her treating physicians attributed to exposure to toxic mold. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] later left the property, which they subsequently demolished because the mold could not be eradicated. [COMPANY_A] retained [COMPANY_B] to provide engineering services to [COMPANY_A] to evaluate mold damage to the property.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: 2007년 9월, [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]는 [PERSON_E]와 [PERSON_F]로부터 주택을 구입하고, 해당 주택에 대해 [COMPANY_A]로부터 주택소유자 보험을 가입했다. 이 보험은 [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B] 및 그들의 미성년 자녀 두 명인 [PERSON_C]와 [PERSON_D]를 보장했으며, 곰팡이로 인해 발생한 재산의 물리적 손실을 보장하는 특약을 포함했다. 이 추가 약정에 따라 [COMPANY_A]는 곰팡이로 인해 발생한 재산의 직접적인 물리적 손실 또는 필요한 추가 비용에 대해 Brunos에게 최대 [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A]를 지급해야 했다. 이 추가 약정은 곰팡이의 존재 여부 또는 수준을 확인하기 위해 공기와 보장 대상 재산을 검사하는 비용을 [COMPANY_A]가 지급하도록 했으며, 곰팡이가 존재하는 경우 곰팡이 제거 비용과 곰팡이에 접근하는 데 필요한 재산의 철거 비용도 지급하도록 했다. 2007년 10월 5일, [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]가 해당 주택으로 이사한 후, [PERSON_A]는 계약자의 도움을 받아 지하실을 개조하기 시작했고 지하실 블록 벽을 덮고 있던 목재 패널의 일부를 제거했다. 패널을 분리한 후, [PERSON_A]는 물이 새는 배관 근처의 블록 벽에서 검은 곰팡이가 있는 두 곳을 발견했다. [PERSON_A]는 [COMPANY_A]에 이를 알리고 주택소유자 보험에 따른 청구를 시작하고 싶다고 말했다. [COMPANY_A]는 곰팡이를 확인하도록 손해사정인을 보냈고, 이틀 후 손해사정인은 [COMPANY_A]가 곰팡이를 조사하고 그 심각성을 판단하며 필요한 복구 범위를 평가하기 위해 고용한 [COMPANY_B] 소속 기술자와 함께 돌아왔다. 손해사정인은 자신에게 권한이 없고 보장 여부가 결정되지 않았다고 말하면서 지급을 거부했다. 곰팡이가 건강에 위험하지 않다는 손해사정인과 기술자의 확언에 근거하여, [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]는 계속 해당 주택에 거주했고 [PERSON_A]는 계속 주택을 개조했다. 10월 동안 [PERSON_A]와 한 계약자는 곰팡이를 제거하려고 시도했으며 추가 패널을 제거했고, 그 결과 더 많은 누수 배관과 추가 곰팡이가 드러났다. [PERSON_A]는 추가로 발견한 내용을 [COMPANY_A]에 알렸다. [COMPANY_A]는 같은 기술자를 보냈고, 그 기술자는 새로 발견된 곰팡이를 육안으로 검사하고 시험을 실시했지만 그 결과를 공개하지 않았다. 10월 동안 가족 구성원 각자는 호흡기 질환을 겪기 시작했고, 그 증상은 다음 몇 달 동안 악화되었다. 2008년 1월까지 [PERSON_B]는 심한 기침, 호흡 및 목을 가다듬는 데 어려움, 극심한 두통이 생겼다. 그 후 [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]는 곰팡이 검사를 위해 비용을 지불했고, 검사 결과 곰팡이가 독성이 있으며 인체 건강에 위험한 것으로 나타났다. 2008년 4월, [COMPANY_A]는 곰팡이 특약에 따라 [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]에게 [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A]를 지급했다. 이후 [PERSON_B]는 인후암과 식도암 진단을 받았고, 담당 의사들은 이를 독성 곰팡이에 노출된 탓으로 보았다. [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]는 이후 해당 주택을 떠났으며, 곰팡이를 제거할 수 없었기 때문에 나중에 그 주택을 철거했다. [COMPANY_A]는 해당 주택의 곰팡이 피해를 평가하기 위해 [COMPANY_A]에 기술 서비스를 제공하도록 [COMPANY_B]를 고용했다.

The defendants included [PERSON_A], the state government, [ORGANIZATION_B], the state health department, and former city emergency managers [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C]. On April 16, 2013, [PERSON_A] authorized a contract to explore an alternative water-delivery system. Plaintiffs alleged that [PERSON_A] and various state officials knew that [LOCATION_B] would be an interim drinking-water source and knew of a 2011 study cautioning against its use as drinking water. On April 25, 2014, under the direction of [PERSON_B] and [ORGANIZATION_B], [LOCATION_A] switched its water source from [ORGANIZATION_A] to [LOCATION_B], and residents began receiving [LOCATION_B] water from their taps. Plaintiffs alleged that this occurred despite warnings that the water-treatment plant was not fit to begin operations and despite a study stating that the plant required facility upgrades costing [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A]. The water-treatment plant’s laboratory and water-quality supervisor warned that the plant was not fit to begin operations. Less than a month after the switch, state officials received complaints about tap-water quality, and in June 2014 residents complained that they were becoming ill after drinking the tap water. On October 13, 2014, [ORGANIZATION_D] discontinued use of [LOCATION_A] water at its [LOCATION_A] plant because of concerns about the water’s corrosive nature. That month, city officials expressed concern about a legionellosis outbreak and possible links between the outbreak and the switch to [LOCATION_B] water. On February 26, 2015, [ORGANIZATION_C] advised [ORGANIZATION_B] that the water supply contained iron at levels too high for testing instruments to measure exactly. That month, [ORGANIZATION_B] was advised that black sediment in some tap water was lead. During this period, state officials did not take significant remedial measures, advised residents that the tap water was safe to drink, and arranged for state employees to drink water from coolers installed in state buildings. Plaintiffs alleged that [ORGANIZATION_B] told [ORGANIZATION_C] that [LOCATION_A] was using a corrosion-control additive while knowing that statement was false. Plaintiffs also alleged that by early March 2015 state officials knew of a public health emergency involving lead poisoning and Legionella bacteria, concealed the health threats, failed to effectively address them, and publicly stated that the water was safe and that there was no widespread lead leaching despite knowing those statements were false. Plaintiffs alleged that through the summer and fall of 2015 state officials continued concealing the health emergency, discrediting reports confirming serious lead contamination, concealing information about lead in the water system, and advising the public that the drinking water was safe despite knowing otherwise. A hospital doctor’s findings reflected a spike in the percentage of [LOCATION_A] children with elevated blood lead levels from blood drawn in the second and third quarters of 2014. In early October 2015, [PERSON_A] acknowledged that the water supply was contaminated with dangerous levels of lead, ordered reconnection to [ORGANIZATION_A] on October 8, 2015, and the reconnection occurred on October 16, 2015. Plaintiffs alleged that although the state and city defendants knew that [LOCATION_B] water was toxic and corrosive, the state defendants authorized the city defendants to supply that water to their property. Plaintiffs alleged that their pipes, service lines, and water heaters were damaged as a result. Plaintiffs alleged that their property values substantially declined after the water crisis became public knowledge. They also alleged that despite knowing the dangers and serious medical risks associated with switching to [LOCATION_B] water, defendants made the switch, misled and deceived the public, and concealed information about the water’s toxicity and corrosiveness. Plaintiffs alleged that using and ingesting [LOCATION_A] water as a result of defendants’ actions caused personal injuries, including neuropathy, sleepiness, gastrointestinal discomfort, dermatological disorders, hair loss, and other symptoms. They also alleged substantial economic losses from medical expenses and lost wages, and that some residents suffered life-threatening and irreversible bodily injuries. [PERSON_A] testified that [ORGANIZATION_B] repeatedly assured him that the water was safe, and that there was no broad consensus that using [LOCATION_B] as a water source would cause a serious public health crisis.

Respondent Pfizer manufactures and markets sertraline hydrochloride as the antidepressant drug, Zoloft; Respondent Roerig is a former division of Pfizer, while Respondent Greenstone is a wholly owned subsidiary of Pfizer that sells an authorized generic version of this medication.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [PERSON_A] worked as a groundskeeper and golf course superintendent for nearly forty years. His work involved regularly applying [PRODUCT_GROUP_A], primarily insecticides and fungicides. During this period, [PERSON_A] kept a detailed record of the products used and their application dates. [PERSON_B], a coworker, testified about how [PERSON_A] applied the pesticides, the products and concentrations used, and the protective gear they wore. Initially, they used only gloves; later, they also used overalls, rubber boots, masks, and eventually disposable protective gear. [PERSON_B] explained that, despite the protective gear, [PERSON_A] was exposed to dust from the pesticide products while opening bags and mixing chemicals. On October 5, 2008, [PERSON_A] arrived at an emergency room with fever, chills, and a cough. A bone marrow biopsy resulted in a diagnosis of Acute Myelogenous Leukemia (AML). Cytogenetic testing revealed significant chromosomal aberrations. [PERSON_A] died on February 2, 2009. [PERSON_C] later opined that [PERSON_A]’s extensive exposure to pesticides raised a high degree of suspicion that the exposure played a significant role in the development of [PERSON_A]’s AML. [PERSON_A]’s expert identified studies stating that the active ingredients in the specific pesticides were genotoxic and caused chromosomal abnormalities. The expert further stated that pesticide or benzene exposure causing AML is associated with abnormalities of the fifth and seventh chromosomes, which initiate a carcinogenic process, and that this pattern was identified in [PERSON_A]’s cytogenetic testing. The expert conducted product-specific analyses of each [PRODUCT_GROUP_A], evaluated the chemical components individually, and concluded that each product contained chemicals that were genotoxic or caused DNA damage and were therefore carcinogenic. The expert concluded that exposure to organophosphate pesticide formulations, individually or in combination, was causally related to an increased risk of leukemia in exposed humans.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: [PERSON_A]는 거의 40년 동안 코스 관리원 및 골프장 관리자로 일했다. [PERSON_A]의 업무에는 [PRODUCT_GROUP_A], 주로 살충제와 살균제를 정기적으로 살포하는 일이 포함되었다. 이 기간 동안 [PERSON_A]는 사용한 제품과 그 살포 날짜를 상세히 기록했다. 동료인 [PERSON_B]는 [PERSON_A]가 살충제를 어떻게 살포했는지, 사용한 제품과 농도, 그리고 그들이 착용한 보호 장비에 대해 증언했다. 처음에는 그들은 장갑만 사용했지만, 나중에는 작업복, 고무 장화, 마스크, 그리고 결국 일회용 보호 장비도 사용했다. [PERSON_B]는 보호 장비에도 불구하고 [PERSON_A]가 봉지를 열고 화학물질을 혼합하는 동안 살충제 제품에서 나온 먼지에 노출되었다고 설명했다. 2008년 10월 5일, [PERSON_A]는 발열, 오한 및 기침 증상으로 응급실에 도착했다. 골수 생검 결과 급성 골수성 백혈병(AML) 진단을 받았다. 세포유전학적 검사에서 상당한 염색체 이상이 확인되었다. [PERSON_A]는 2009년 2월 2일 사망했다. [PERSON_C]는 나중에 [PERSON_A]의 광범위한 살충제 노출로 인해 그 노출이 [PERSON_A]의 AML 발병에 중요한 역할을 했다는 강한 의심이 제기된다는 의견을 밝혔다. [PERSON_A]의 전문가는 특정 살충제의 유효성분이 유전독성이 있고 염색체 이상을 유발한다고 밝힌 연구들을 제시했다. 전문가는 또한 AML을 유발하는 살충제 또는 벤젠 노출은 제5번 및 제7번 염색체의 이상과 관련되어 있으며, 이러한 이상이 발암 과정을 시작하고, 이 패턴이 [PERSON_A]의 세포유전학적 검사에서 확인되었다고 말했다. 전문가는 각 [PRODUCT_GROUP_A]에 대해 제품별 분석을 실시하고 화학 성분을 개별적으로 평가한 후, 각 제품에 유전독성이 있거나 DNA 손상을 유발하는 화학물질이 포함되어 있으며 따라서 발암성이라고 결론 내렸다. 전문가는 유기인계 살충제 제형에 개별적으로 또는 복합적으로 노출되는 것이 노출된 사람의 백혈병 위험 증가와 인과관계가 있다고 결론 내렸다.

[PERSON_A]의 전문가는 특정 살충제의 유효성분이 유전독성이 있고 염색체 이상을 유발한다고 밝힌 연구들을 제시했다. 전문가는 또한 AML을 유발하는 살충제 또는 벤젠 노출은 제5번 및 제7번 염색체의 이상과 관련되어 있으며, 이러한 이상이 발암 과정을 시작하고, 이 패턴이 [PERSON_A]의 세포유전학적 검사에서 확인되었다고 말했다. 전문가는 각 [PRODUCT_GROUP_A]에 대해 제품별 분석을 실시하고 화학 성분을 개별적으로 평가한 후, 각 제품에 유전독성이 있거나 DNA 손상을 유발하는 화학물질이 포함되어 있으며 따라서 발암성이라고 결론 내렸다. 전문가는 유기인계 살충제 제형에 개별적으로 또는 복합적으로 노출되는 것이 노출된 사람의 백혈병 위험 증가와 인과관계가 있다고 결론 내렸다.
neutral_fact_source: [PERSON_A] worked as a groundskeeper and golf course superintendent for nearly forty years. His work involved regularly applying [PRODUCT_GROUP_A], primarily insecticides and fungicides. During this period, [PERSON_A] kept a detailed record of the products used and their application dates. [PERSON_B], a coworker, testified about how [PERSON_A] applied the pesticides, the products and concentrations used, and the protective gear they wore. Initially, they used only gloves; later, they also used overalls, rubber boots, masks, and eventually disposable protective gear. [PERSON_B] explained that, despite the protective gear, [PERSON_A] was exposed to dust from the pesticide products while opening bags and mixing chemicals. On October 5, 2008, [PERSON_A] arrived at an emergency room with fever, chills, and a cough. A bone marrow biopsy resulted in a diagnosis of Acute Myelogenous Leukemia (AML). Cytogenetic testing revealed significant chromosomal aberrations. [PERSON_A] died on February 2, 2009. [PERSON_C] later opined that [PERSON_A]’s extensive exposure to pesticides raised a high degree of suspicion that the exposure played a significant role in the development of [PERSON_A]’s AML. [PERSON_A]’s executor brought claims against [COMPANY_GROUP_A], whose products [PERSON_A] had applied during his career. The remaining manufacturers made fifteen pesticide products to which [PERSON_A] was exposed. [PERSON_A] developed AML, had significant chromosomal aberrations identified through cytogenetic testing, and died on February 2, 2009. [PERSON_A]’s expert identified studies stating that the active ingredients in the specific pesticides were genotoxic and caused chromosomal abnormalities. The expert further stated that pesticide or benzene exposure causing AML is associated with abnormalities of the fifth and seventh chromosomes, which initiate a carcinogenic process, and that this pattern was identified in [PERSON_A]’s cytogenetic testing. The expert conducted product-specific analyses of each [PRODUCT_GROUP_A], evaluated the chemical components individually, and concluded that each product contained chemicals that were genotoxic or caused DNA damage and were therefore carcinogenic. The expert concluded that exposure to organophosphate pesticide formulations, individually or in combination, was causally related to an increased risk of leukemia in exposed humans.

[PERSON_A] was injured during a training exercise on October 19, 1995, while training with tactical units from other institutions. Five training exercises were conducted that day as simulations to prepare officers for inmate disturbances or riots; [PERSON_A] completed the first two exercises without injury. During the third exercise, called the "angry crowd exercise," [PERSON_A] and his unit role-played as inmates while other units role-played as guards. In prior exercises, batons were wrapped in Styrofoam and officers wore protective pads; during this exercise, unpadded batons were used and officers wore only helmets. [PERSON_A] testified that someone grabbed him and struck his left arm at full force; after he shouted the code word intended to stop the activity, he continued to be struck with unpadded batons. He was later seen in an emergency room, where he complained of pain in his left arm, shoulder, and neck. The tactical-unit commander testified that he knew batons would be used but did not expect full-force strikes; he expected that a participant might get "banged up" or "hurt." He learned of [PERSON_A]'s injury at the end of the last exercise when [PERSON_A] reported being struck in the arm. Medical records documented injuries to [PERSON_A]'s forearm, neck, and/or shoulder. He underwent cervical spine procedures on February 5, 1996, and July 14, 1997, and shoulder surgeries on May 16, 1996, and January 30, 1997. The record states that he had not previously participated in exercises involving full-force strikes or unpadded batons. [PERSON_A] testified that he did not expect a full-force altercation during the exercise and did not expect or consent to being struck with an unpadded baton at full force.

He was later seen in an emergency room, where he complained of pain in his left arm, shoulder, and neck. The tactical-unit commander testified that he knew batons would be used but did not expect full-force strikes; he expected that a participant might get "banged up" or "hurt." He learned of [PERSON_A]'s injury at the end of the last exercise when [PERSON_A] reported being struck in the arm. Medical records documented injuries to [PERSON_A]'s forearm, neck, and/or shoulder. The record states that he had not previously participated in exercises involving full-force strikes or unpadded batons. [PERSON_A] testified that he did not expect a full-force altercation during the exercise and did not expect or consent to being struck with an unpadded baton at full force.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [COMPANY_B] was a professional consulting engineering firm, [PERSON_B] was its president, and [PERSON_A] had worked for [COMPANY_B] as a professional land surveyor for many years and headed its survey department during the relevant events. In 2006, [PERSON_A] regularly accepted surveying work independent of his work for [COMPANY_B] with [PERSON_B]’s permission, used his own equipment for that work, and performed it outside his 40-hour workweek for [COMPANY_B]. [COMPANY_B] did not bill clients for work [PERSON_A] performed independently, which included elevation surveys. [PERSON_C] was one of the owners of [COMPANY_A], a company that sold medical equipment for use by elderly people and people with disabilities. Around September 2006, [PERSON_C] contacted [COMPANY_B] about surveying a property [COMPANY_A] had purchased in [LOCATION_A]. [COMPANY_B] sent [PERSON_A] to speak with [PERSON_C] about that property. After [PERSON_A] began work there, [PERSON_C] asked him to perform an elevation survey and complete an elevation certificate for property in [LOCATION_B]. [PERSON_A] made two trips to the [LOCATION_B] property and worked approximately 10 to 15 hours on the survey. He used his own surveying equipment and did not drive a company vehicle. On the elevation certificate, he listed his title as “Land Surveyor,” left “Company Name” blank, and listed his home address. He gave [PERSON_C] a handwritten invoice that listed his personal address and did not refer to [COMPANY_B]. [COMPANY_B] did not issue an invoice for [PERSON_A]’s work at the [LOCATION_B] property and was not paid for that project. Twenty days after [PERSON_A] completed the elevation certificate, [PERSON_C] signed a check dated November 1, 2006, from [COMPANY_C] payable to [PERSON_A] for [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A]. [PERSON_A] testified that he thought the check paid for his work at the [LOCATION_B] property but could not confirm that, while [PERSON_C] testified that he did not know what the check paid for. After completing the work, [PERSON_A] realized that he had made a 30.48-meter error on the flood-elevation certificate: he recorded a base flood elevation of approximately 180.75 meters instead of approximately 211.84 meters for Buildings 1 through 5. [PERSON_C] alleges that this error caused the certificates to incorrectly state that the [LOCATION_B] property was outside the 100-year flood plain. [PERSON_B] testified that [PERSON_A] was acting independently when he worked on the [LOCATION_B] property, that the work was not a project of [COMPANY_B], that [COMPANY_B] was not paid for it, that [COMPANY_B] did not send [PERSON_C] or [COMPANY_A] an invoice for it, and that [PERSON_B] did not know about the work until months later, when [PERSON_A] spoke with him about the error.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: [COMPANY_B]는 전문 컨설팅 엔지니어링 회사였고, [PERSON_B]는 그 회사의 사장이었으며, [PERSON_A]는 여러 해 동안 [COMPANY_B]에서 전문 측량사로 근무했고 관련 사건이 발생한 기간 동안 그 회사의 측량 부서를 이끌었다. 2006년에 [PERSON_A]는 [PERSON_B]의 허락을 받아 [COMPANY_B]에서의 업무와 독립적으로 측량 업무를 정기적으로 수락했고, 그 업무에 자신의 장비를 사용했으며, [COMPANY_B]에서의 주 40시간 근무 외에 그 업무를 수행했다. [COMPANY_B]는 [PERSON_A]가 독립적으로 수행한 업무에 대해 고객들에게 청구하지 않았으며, 그 업무에는 표고 측량이 포함되었다. [PERSON_C]는 노인과 장애인이 사용하기 위한 의료 장비를 판매하는 회사인 [COMPANY_A]의 소유자 중 한 명이었다. 2006년 9월경, [PERSON_C]는 [COMPANY_A]가 [LOCATION_A]에서 매입한 부동산의 측량과 관련하여 [COMPANY_B]에 연락했다. [COMPANY_B]는 [PERSON_A]를 보내 해당 부동산에 관해 [PERSON_C]와 이야기하게 했다. [PERSON_A]가 그곳에서 업무를 시작한 후, [PERSON_C]는 그에게 [LOCATION_B]의 부동산에 대한 표고 측량을 하고 표고 증명서를 작성해 달라고 요청했다. [PERSON_A]는 [LOCATION_B]의 부동산에 두 차례 방문했고 측량에 약 10~15시간을 들였다. 그는 자신의 측량 장비를 사용했으며 회사 차량을 운전하지 않았다. 표고 증명서에는 자신의 직함을 “Land Surveyor”로 기재하고, “Company Name”은 공란으로 두었으며, 자신의 집 주소를 기재했다. 그는 [PERSON_C]에게 자신의 개인 주소가 기재되어 있고 [COMPANY_B]를 언급하지 않은 자필 청구서를 건넸다. [COMPANY_B]는 [LOCATION_B]의 부동산에서 [PERSON_A]가 수행한 업무에 대한 청구서를 발행하지 않았고 그 프로젝트에 대한 대금도 받지 않았다. [PERSON_A]가 표고 증명서를 작성한 지 20일 후, [PERSON_C]는 [COMPANY_C]가 [PERSON_A]에게 [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A]를 지급하도록 하는 2006년 11월 1일자 수표에 서명했다. [PERSON_A]는 그 수표가 자신이 [LOCATION_B]의 부동산에서 수행한 업무에 대한 대금이라고 생각했지만 이를 확인할 수는 없었다고 증언했으며, [PERSON_C]는 그 수표가 무엇에 대한 대금인지 몰랐다고 증언했다. 업무를 완료한 후, [PERSON_A]는 홍수 표고 증명서에서 30.48미터의 오류를 범했다는 것을 알게 되었다. 즉, 건물 1부터 5까지에 대해 약 211.84미터가 아니라 약 180.75미터의 기준 홍수 표고를 기록했다. [PERSON_C]는 이 오류로 인해 증명서에 [LOCATION_B]의 부동산이 100년 빈도 홍수 평야 밖에 있는 것으로 잘못 기재되었다고 주장한다. [PERSON_B]는 [PERSON_A]가 [LOCATION_B]의 부동산에서 일할 때 독립적으로 행동했으며, 그 업무는 [COMPANY_B]의 프로젝트가 아니었고, [COMPANY_B]는 그 대금을 받지 않았으며, [COMPANY_B]는 그 업무에 대한 청구서를 [PERSON_C]나 [COMPANY_A]에 보내지 않았고, [PERSON_B]는 [PERSON_A]가 그 오류에 관해 자신과 이야기한 몇 달 후까지 그 업무를 알지 못했다고 증언했다.

[PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] alleged that [PRODUCT_A] and [PRODUCT_B] came from [PRODUCT_C] used by [COMPANY_D], and that [COMPANY_A], [COMPANY_B], and [COMPANY_C] manufactured those paints. [PERSON_A] was formerly employed by [COMPANY_D]. [PERSON_C] testified that he did not know how often [PERSON_A] was in the Exterior Finish Booth, how close [PERSON_A] was to the Prime Booth or paint sprayers, what ventilation equipment was used, or the frequency and level of [PERSON_A]'s exposure. [PERSON_C] based his causation testimony on [PERSON_A]'s general statement that he was in and out of the area regularly. [PERSON_C] reviewed only one pulmonary function test and did not review [PERSON_A]'s other medical records for the relevant period. [PERSON_C] testified that [PERSON_A]'s current respiratory problems could have been an aggravation of preexisting asthma that existed before [PERSON_A]'s employment by [COMPANY_D], exacerbated by nonspecific irritants regardless of exposure at [COMPANY_D] to the chemicals at issue. [PERSON_C] identified three potential causes for [PERSON_A]'s alleged aggravation of preexisting asthma: exposure to [PRODUCT_B], exposure to [PRODUCT_A], or chronic exposure to unidentified nonspecific irritants. [PERSON_D] testified that heating materials coated with activated polyurethane and epoxy resin products, including heating from welding, produces decomposition products that can include components of the paints, phthalic acid anhydride and similar anhydrides, and isocyanate monomers. [COMPANY_A], [COMPANY_B], and [COMPANY_C] disputed that [PERSON_D]'s affidavit established that [PERSON_A] was actually exposed to [PRODUCT_A] or [PRODUCT_B], or that such exposure caused [PERSON_A]'s breathing problems.

source_fact_units.model_source_span: She stepped into a depressed area of the sidewalk, lost her balance, tripped on a raised and uneven area of bricks next to the depression, and fell forward. As a result, she fractured her wrist, necessitating two surgeries. It is undisputed that the raised portion of the sidewalk was less than two inches and that defendant, the city of Lansing, maintained this sidewalk. Plaintiff sued defendant under the highway exception to governmental immunity, alleging that defendant had breached its duty under MCL 691.1402(1) to maintain the sidewalk in reasonable repair. Defendant answered, raising as an affirmative defense the two-inch rule of MCL 691.1402a(2).

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [PERSON_A] purchased [VEHICLE_A] from [COMPANY_A], a used-car dealership that had immediately purchased the vehicle from [COMPANY_B] after a trade-in. Several months after acquiring [VEHICLE_A], [PERSON_A] was involved in an automobile accident. [PERSON_A] suffered severe injuries in the automobile accident. [PERSON_A] alleged that [COMPANY_B] failed to attach a revised airbag warning label to [VEHICLE_A]. [PERSON_A] alleged that the revised airbag warning label would have prevented the injuries suffered in the accident. [COMPANY_B] had previously serviced [VEHICLE_A] regularly. [COMPANY_B] asserted that the existing warning label was not inadequate or defective and that the replacement warning label applied only to vehicles manufactured after 1997, not to [VEHICLE_B]. It was uncontested that the applicable rule did not require manufacturers or dealerships to install revised warning labels in vehicles manufactured before February 1997. [PERSON_A] admitted in the pleadings that, at the time of the accident, the airbags functioned as designed. Both parties conceded that [COMPANY_B] never worked on the airbags.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: [PERSON_A]는 중고차 판매업체인 [COMPANY_A]로부터 [VEHICLE_A]를 구입했으며, [COMPANY_A]는 보상판매 후 해당 차량을 [COMPANY_B]로부터 즉시 구입했다. [VEHICLE_A]를 취득한 지 몇 달 후, [PERSON_A]는 자동차 사고에 연루되었다. [PERSON_A]는 자동차 사고로 중상을 입었다. [PERSON_A]는 [COMPANY_B]가 [VEHICLE_A]에 개정된 에어백 경고 라벨을 부착하지 않았다고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]는 개정된 에어백 경고 라벨이 부착되었더라면 사고에서 입은 부상을 방지했을 것이라고 주장했다. [COMPANY_B]는 이전에 [VEHICLE_A]를 정기적으로 정비했다. [COMPANY_B]는 기존 경고 라벨이 부적절하거나 결함이 있는 것이 아니었으며, 교체용 경고 라벨은 1997년 이후 제조된 차량에만 적용되고 [VEHICLE_B]에는 적용되지 않는다고 주장했다. 적용되는 규정이 1997년 2월 이전에 제조된 차량에 개정된 경고 라벨을 설치하도록 제조업체나 판매업체에 요구하지 않았다는 점에는 다툼이 없었다. [PERSON_A]는 서면에서 사고 당시 에어백이 설계된 대로 작동했다고 인정했다. 양측 당사자는 [COMPANY_B]가 에어백을 작업한 적이 전혀 없다는 점을 인정했다.

aligned_fact_units.neutral_en: [PERSON_B] was the attending physician and [PERSON_C] was the surgical resident who performed the surgery on [PERSON_A]. [PERSON_A] underwent a laparoscopic hysterectomy. [PERSON_A] suffered a severed colon during the procedure. The injury occurred during the incision and before insertion of the laparoscope. [PERSON_D] testified that the procedure begins with an incision at the base of the bellybutton and removal of layers of the abdominal wall. [PERSON_D] testified that, before cutting the peritoneum, the surgeon should look through it to identify the organs and anatomical structures beneath it; after that step, the surgeon makes a cut of approximately 3 to 4 millimeters into the peritoneum. [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_C] did not look through the peritoneum before cutting into it, according to [PERSON_E]’s acknowledgment and [PERSON_C]’s testimony. [PERSON_E] testified that the tissue is often too thick to see through and that, for an overweight patient, it is almost always impossible to see through the peritoneum. [PERSON_C] testified that she usually did not try to pull up and look through the peritoneum for a patient with a high body mass index, and that [PERSON_A]’s body mass index was in the 30s. [PERSON_E] testified that a colon injury can occur as a complication during this procedure and that the occurrence of the injury alone did not identify how it happened. [PERSON_E] testified that an incision through the peritoneum can injure the large or small intestine and characterized the colon injury as a complication of the procedure. [PERSON_D] testified that, in a laparoscopic hysterectomy, complications can occur during surgery and most arise during entry into the peritoneum.
aligned_fact_units.neutral_ko: [PERSON_B]는 담당 의사였고 [PERSON_C]는 [PERSON_A]에 대한 수술을 시행한 외과 전공의였다. [PERSON_A]는 복강경 자궁적출술을 받았다. [PERSON_A]는 해당 시술 중 결장이 절단되는 손상을 입었다. 그 손상은 절개 중에, 그리고 복강경을 삽입하기 전에 발생했다. [PERSON_D]는 해당 시술이 배꼽 밑부분을 절개하고 복벽의 층들을 제거하는 것으로 시작한다고 증언했다. [PERSON_D]는 복막을 절개하기 전에 의사가 복막을 통해 그 아래에 있는 장기와 해부학적 구조를 확인해야 하며, 그 단계 후에 의사가 복막에 약 3~4밀리미터 깊이로 절개한다고 증언했다. [PERSON_E]의 인정과 [PERSON_C]의 증언에 따르면, [PERSON_B]와 [PERSON_C]는 복막을 절개하기 전에 복막을 통해 들여다보지 않았다. [PERSON_E]는 조직이 너무 두꺼워서 들여다볼 수 없는 경우가 많으며, 과체중 환자의 경우 복막을 통해 들여다보는 것이 거의 항상 불가능하다고 증언했다. [PERSON_C]는 체질량지수가 높은 환자의 경우 보통 복막을 들어 올려 들여다보려고 하지 않았으며, [PERSON_A]의 체질량지수는 30대였다고 증언했다. [PERSON_E]는 결장 손상이 이 시술 과정에서 합병증으로 발생할 수 있으며, 손상이 발생했다는 사실만으로 그 발생 경위를 특정할 수는 없다고 증언했다. [PERSON_E]는 복막을 절개하는 과정에서 대장이나 소장이 손상될 수 있으며, 결장 손상을 해당 시술의 합병증이라고 표현했다. [PERSON_D]는 수술 중 합병증이 발생할 수 있으며, 복강경 자궁적출술에서는 대부분의 합병증이 복막으로 진입하는 과정에서 발생한다고 증언했다.
